The woman, Alice Huang, is affiliated with a cloud company and an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, which has been accused of helping restricted Chinese companies acquire Nvidia AI chips.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/trump-ir.title: Trump says renewed Iran strikes ‘highly unlikely’ if talks progress but warns he could still strike
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/trump-ir.author: Garrett Downs
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/trump-ir.text:
President Donald Trump said renewed U.S. attacks on Iran are ‘highly unlikely’ if negotiations produce a strong agreement on Iran’s nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The conflict has continued in intermittent bursts of fighting and limited strikes separated by ceasefires and negotiations.

Trump said three U.S. aircraft carriers were positioned in the region and that the U.S. had identified Iranian bridges and power plants as potential targets.

President Donald Trump said he is “highly unlikely” to restart open war with Iran, but warned he could still strike the country as Washington tries to reach a deal with Tehran to end the conflict.

The now more than eight-month-old war, which stoked inflation and sent oil
 prices surging, has seen repeated bursts of fighting separated by ceasefires and peace talks for months. It was widely speculated that Trump might restart open conflict after the midterm elections, where his Republican Party lost badly to Democrats.

Trump’s comments came during an interview with CNN, where he said restarting the war is unlikely as long as talks to constrain Iran’s nuclear program and reopen the Strait of Hormuz make progress.

“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said. “The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary. They’re a failing nation.”

Trump, however, left the door open for additional strikes if he deems it necessary. The president reiterated his threats to strike bridges and power plants in Iran if the war restarts.

“I’ve got three aircraft carriers here. The other one just arrived. We have three. They’re fully locked and loaded,” the president said. “We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour.”

An end to the war and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would likely ease oil prices, though finding a truce has proven difficult. All previous attempts to end the war and reopen the strait have been met with disappointment.

Trump is likely to come under increased pressure to end the conflict, however, now that Democrats have won control of both the House and the Senate. Some Republicans are also likely to be eager for an end to the war, given the role high gas prices played in their drubbing at the ballot box.

The president has demanded Iran fully open the Strait of Hormuz and agree to never develop a nuclear weapon as part of any deal.

Later in the day on Truth Social, Trump posted that “Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

“Coupled with history’s greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!” he said.

Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday, describing it as an initiative aimed at “preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea.”

The U.S. has maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports for months.
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/trump-ir.summary: President Donald Trump said he is ‘highly unlikely’ to restart open war with Iran. He said he could still strike the country as Washington tries to reach a deal with Tehran to end the conflict. The conflict has continued in intermittent bursts of fighting and limited strikes separated by ceasefires and negotiations.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/democrat.title: Democrats amp up Trump investigation threats, Blanche counters he may probe lawmakers
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/democrat.author: Garrett Downs
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/democrat.text:
Democrats are preparing broad oversight of the Trump administration and private companies tied to it after winning control of both chambers.

Blanche said DOJ investigations of Democratic lawmakers “could” occur depending on what was said.

Democrats have won control of Congress, but incoming committee chairs gain formal gavels and subpoena authority when the new Congress convenes in January.

Top Democrats are ramping up oversight of the Trump administration and businesses it has partnered with, while Attorney General Todd Blanche warned he could counterinvestigate lawmakers conducting probes.

Democrats romped to majorities in both the House and the Senate during Tuesday’s midterm elections, putting them in position to seize control of committee gavels and subpoena power in January. The electoral rout leaves Democrats with at least 54 Senate seats and 254 seats in the House of Representatives as votes continue to be counted in several states.

Democrats vowed to investigate both President Donald Trump’s White House and businesses that have worked with the administration. CNBC reported on Thursday that Democrats are expected to take an aggressive approach to probing businesses, especially those companies with ties to the Trump family. The technology, cryptocurrency and prediction market industries, among others, could immediately be in the crosshairs.

“If you’ve been making your profits by cheating American families and scamming your investors, you better get ready for some investigations — serious ones,” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the incoming chair of the Senate Banking Committee, on CBS’ “Face the Nation” on Sunday. “The American people are just damn sick of this.”

Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, whom the Senate narrowly confirmed as the nation’s top cop earlier this year, took umbrage at the Democrats’ plans for investigations and said he may launch his own investigations against members of Congress.

“There could be,” Blanche said Sunday when pressed on CNN’s “State of the Union” about whether the administration will counterinvestigate Democrats.

“When the threats become so vile and so dangerous that you are telling people in college that they better be careful if they want to work in the Trump administration because somebody will come after them, at some point you have to draw the line.”

Blanche was referring to comments made by Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who said during a University of Chicago event that she wants “young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration?’...I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want. And so let me avoid participating in that.’ I want that deterrence message sent.”

Trump has ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats over the comments.

Blanche also took aim at Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the likely incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee — appearing to caution lawmakers who sit on the panel. Garcia warned the administration and business leaders to “lawyer up” after the election.

“I would be very worried if I was a member on that committee,” Blanche said.

Garcia shot back, saying on CNN: “What Todd Blanche is doing right now is a threat.”

“He’s trying to stop us from doing real oversight,” Garcia said. “He is the person that should be reading the Constitution, because the Constitution makes it very clear that it’s our job in Congress to conduct oversight of the executive and the administration.”
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/democrat.summary: Democrats have won control of Congress, but incoming committee chairs gain formal gavels and subpoena authority when the new Congress convenes in January. Attorney General Todd Blanche said DOJ investigations of Democratic lawmakers ‘could’ occur depending on what was said.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/jensen-h.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/jensen-h.author: Kamaron McNair
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/jensen-h.text:
U.S. intelligence reportedly assessed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to gather information on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia had said Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were ordinary customer contacts and that no sensitive trade secrets or national-security information were shared.

Three Republican House committee chairs asked Huang to appear for a joint closed-door briefing on Nov. 18, while Democratic lawmakers separately called for an investigation or testimony.

Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for congressional investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it is opening an independent investigation into Huang’s involvement with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.

In a memo to Nvidia
 staff on Sunday, Huang disclosed he had been intimate with the woman, but the affair was not mentioned in the board’s statement. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating, the board said.

“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” the board said in its statement.

“Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” the company told CNBC in a statement.

Lawmakers have been calling for an investigation into the relationship and are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about it.

“The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I’m convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn’t corrupt,” Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. “Congress will investigate and get answers.”

Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.

Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday asking him to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China’s] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang.

Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive, the Times first reported on Friday. Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the memo’s creation, the Times reported Sunday, citing people briefed on the matter. The State Department and the White House did not immediately respond to CNBC’s request for comment.

When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. “Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed,” Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.

Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO’s interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia’s customers, the Times reported.

Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump’s Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.

Cornyn called the report “outrageous” in his post on X.

Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.

Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC’s request for comment.
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/jensen-h.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been accused of having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The company says it is opening an independent investigation into the relationship. Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for congressional investigations.

https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot begins the hard work of forging a coalition government
https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/.author: FRANCE 24
https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/.text:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government Sunday evening.

Complex coalition negotiations still lie ahead, but it marked a significant step in the former military chief's effort to oust Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, after neither bloc emerged from the October 27 parliamentary elections with a majority.

“I hope with all my heart that whatever government is formed will lead to unity, connection and healing among all segments of our people – for our very existence depends on it, and we have only one country,” Herzog said at the ceremony at the presidential residence in Jerusalem.

The announcement doesn't guarantee that Eisenkot, a former army chief, will become the next prime minister. He has up to six weeks to form a coalition government by securing alliances.

Herzog said that in consultations with the parties, a majority of members of parliament, known as the Knesset, supported giving Eisenkot this task.

At Sunday's ceremony, Eisenkot promised to give the country leadership that people can trust, that will act in the interests of the public and that represents all parts of society.

“An absolute majority of Knesset members representing the Israeli public support change,” he said. “I intend to navigate the situation with patience, humility, composure and a deep commitment to a Jewish, equal, liberal, and secure Israel.”

Among the possible kingmakers – and most politically fraught potential allies – are the Arab-led parties. They made historic gains in the election thanks to high voter turnout among Israel's Arab citizens.

Only one Arab party, Ra’am, has ever joined a governing coalition, in 2021. Ra’am has said it will support Eisenkot, but the party does not have enough seats on its own to give Eisenkot a parliamentary majority.

READ MORE
Israel's Arab list backs Eisenkot as Netanyahu loses ultra-Orthodox support

Breaking with decades of precedent, the second Arab-led party, the Joint List, has offered to support Eisenkot from outside the coalition to end Netanyahu’s grip on power.

But that cooperation is fraught for both sides. For the Joint List, it would mean backing a government unlikely to end Israel’s wars or curb the creeping annexation of the occupied West Bank through illegal settlements. For Eisenkot and other opposition parties, it would mean aligning with parties that not only criticise Israel’s policies but reject its identity as a Jewish state.

One of Eisenkot’s partners, the more conservative Yisrael Beytenu party, already has said it will not join a coalition with Arab-led parties.

Eisenkot has laid out four conditions for parties that want to join him. They must recognise Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, accept its declaration of independence, support military, national or civil service for all citizens, and declare the Hamas militant group a terrorist group. It remains unclear whether his would-be Arab partners are ready to accept these conditions.

Furthermore, Netanyahu has repeatedly asserted unsubstantiated claims that the election was “stolen” by Arab parties. In a pressure tactic on Eisenkot, he says any alliance with these parties would be an act of betrayal.

Israel’s Shin Bet security agency has launched an investigation into possible foreign interference in the vote, but the country’s Central Elections Committee – and Herzog – say the vote was valid and even if wrongdoing is found, it did not have a significant impact on the electoral results.

Eisenkot has vowed to form a government as quickly as possible. But each likely scenario appears to entail compromises or broken promises.

Aside from seeking the support of the Arab-led parties, Eisenkot has two options: a power-sharing agreement with Netanyahu or an agreement with the ultra-Orthodox parties, which demand military exemptions for their community.

READ MORE
Israel's Eisenkot claims 'progress' in coalition talks as opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft

Eisenkot and his partners made equal military service a central part of their campaign. Specifically, they are seeking an end to the long-standing draft exemptions.

The religious parties, which were part of Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition, want to preserve them, calling them essential to their lifestyle of religious study. But the exemptions have grown especially controversial among the broader public during the past three years of war.

Anticipating its position as a swing vote, the ultra-Orthodox party United Torah Judaism has left the door open to cooperating with Eisenkot.

The former military chief also appealed to Netanyahu's right-wing Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join a government led by himself as prime minister.

"My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment," he said.

Eisenkot has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible two-week extension from the president. If he is unable to form a government, Netanyahu could then be given a chance to put together a coalition. If Netanyahu is also unable to do so, the country would return to elections early next spring.

Israel’s new members of Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday evening. Netanyahu and his cabinet will remain in office in a caretaker capacity, with limited powers, until a coalition is formed.

Despite tenuous ceasefires, Israel's military continues to fight Hamas militants in the rubble of Gaza and Iran-aligned Hezbollah militants in Lebanon, where Israel has occupied swathes of the south.

The the war the country launched alongside the US against Iran also shows no sign of ending.

(FRANCE 24 with AP and AFP)
https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/.summary: Gadi Eisenkot has up to six weeks to form a coalition government by securing alliances. Arab-led parties made historic gains in the election thanks to high voter turnout.

https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261.title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities say
https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261.author: FRANCE 24
https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261.text:
A small boat carrying migrants sank off northwestern Senegal killing 34 people in the latest tragedy along the dangerous Atlantic Ocean route from Africa to Europe, the authorities said Sunday.

It was the latest disaster on a route where thousands have died in recent years trying to reach Spain's Canary Islands from West Africa.

An initial statement from the Senegalese interior ministry said 21 bodies and only one survivor had been recovered following the sinking, but that those numbers were provisional as the search continued.

Later Sunday however, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) said the toll now stood at 34 at least, a figure confirmed by Action for Human Rights and Friendship (ADHA) in a statement to AFP.

An "indeterminate number" of people were reported missing, APS added.

Media reports said the pirogue-type flat-bottom boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.

However Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegal's main migrant aid association Boza Fii, told AFP that "the sinking occurred on Friday".

The nationalities of all the victims had not been confirmed "as the search is ongoing", he said.

"But the bodies recovered yesterday (Saturday) are Senegalese," he added.

Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye wrote on social media Sunday that "all state authorities and resources have been mobilised to locate those who have gone missing, provide care for the survivors and support families".

He also pledged to crack down on people organising the risky voyages.

“No one should set out with the sea as their only horizon. We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here,” he said.

Thousands of people from West Africa try each year to reach Europe on the perilous Atlantic route.

Senegalese authorities also said they had intercepted 142 migrants on Friday who were on a similar small boat aiming to reach Spain.

The group included 23 women, two babies and two other children, and were from Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria, according to police.

Senegal's interior ministry stressed "its determination to combat people smuggling networks, notably through strengthened cooperation with neighbouring countries" in a statement Sunday.

The country's interior minister would visit the region where the accident happened to meet families of the victims and express condolences on behalf of the state, it added.

Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro declared an emergency on Saturday after a surge in migrant boat arrivals.

Since the start of November, El Hierro authorities said more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard around 30 boats.

Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco have stepped up maritime patrols around departure points for small boats, forcing them to head further south towards the coasts of Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea, which prolongs the duration of the already hazardous crossing.

(FRANCE 24 with AFP and AP)
https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261.summary: Senegalese authorities say 34 people died in the sinking of a small boat carrying migrants. The boat capsized off the Loumpoul dunes in Kebemer department, between Dakar and Saint-Louis. The death toll from the sinking now stands at 34, the Senegalesese Press Agency says.

https://www.france24.com/en/sport/202611.title: Spain's Alcaraz beats error-prone Shelton to win Paris Masters for first time
https://www.france24.com/en/sport/202611.author: FRANCE 24
https://www.france24.com/en/sport/202611.text:
Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

"Coming here every year, not finding my best tennis but we never gave up," Alcaraz said after being handed the trophy for the first time by former Paris Masters winner Boris Becker.

"We had really painful losses here and we always said try again," he added with a smile.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year – only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

Coming into Paris on the back of winning the 500-level title in Vienna, Alcaraz has won his last nine matches.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route – this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level – both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

Serving at 1-2 in the first set, Alcaraz flirted with danger as he offered up four break points, but dug in to secure the hold when Shelton misfired at the end of a seven-minute long game.

Shelton then found himself two break points down in the seventh game but responded with a perfect drop volley and blistering passing shot to bring up deuce, before holding and keeping his nose in front.

Although both players threatened on the other's serve and drew repeated gasps from the crowd with some audacious shot-making, the opener nonetheless required a tie-break to separate them.

A Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard's side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz's serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be "ten out of ten" when facing Shelton's serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard's finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

The Australian Open champion has now won three ⁠titles since the heartbreak at Flushing Meadows as he looks to end the year on a bright ⁠note at ​the ATP Finals starting next Sunday, followed by the Davis Cup finals later this month.

"Today, it was one ‌of the toughest challenges we have in tennis right now, facing ⁠Ben Shelton," Alcaraz said after the match.

"He is doing better ​and better with every tournament so it's going to be ‌even tougher facing him. So I'm just really happy that I found the way."

Usman Khawaja leads his team off the field during a Sheffield Shield game in 2016. (Getty Images: Paul Kane)

Usman Khawaja says ball tampering was common at Sheffield Shield level, with Victoria the best at it.

Khawaja said one player went as far as using super glue in his towel to rough the ball up.

Khawaja's book Sabr is set to be released to the public on Tuesday.

Usman Khawaja says ball tampering was common at Sheffield Shield level and the Victorians were the best at it.

Following his explosive claims that all Australian players and staff knew about the ball tampering during the South Africa tour of 2018, Khawaja has made a further claim that tampering was common at Sheffield Shield level.

"The Victorians were probably the best at it. The MCG used to be dead and flat. Reverse swing and a bit of spin was the only way you could win a game there," Khawaja wrote in his new book Sabr, which is set to be released to the public on Tuesday.

"I personally never tampered with a ball — in terms of scratching it or anything — but I knew everything that was going on and I wasn't against it which made me complicit.

"The Victorians of that 2000s and 2010s era were genius at it. Throwing it into the wicket and doing other dark arts to rough it up and make the shiny side relatively shinier. It was all fair game."

Khawaja named former Australian ODI fast bowler Mick Lewis as someone who was caught out changing the state of the ball.

Mick Lewis was caught raking the ball across concrete in 2016. (Supplied)

"It was no surprise when, years later, Victoria's bowling coach, Micky Lewis, was caught on cameras scraping the ball in the gutter when it got hit for a boundary. This kind of stuff was very normal," Khawaja wrote.

"There were plenty of times we hoped a spinner got hit for a six so someone could fetch the ball and scrub it while no one was watching and we could reverse swing it.

"To be honest, everyone knew what was going on in those teams I played in growing up. So whether you did it personally or not we were all complicit. The world game was the same. Reverse swing on those older, flatter Test wickets was how you won the matches, come day four and five.''

The former Australian Test batter also claimed an unnamed player had used super glue to tamper with the ball.

Darren Lehmann reacts to bombshell ball tampering claims.

"One of the players had super glue on his towel,'' Khawaja wrote about his first year in Sheffield Shield.

"He'd get the ball on the rough side and scrub it against the dried-up super glue. It worked a treat and the ball would always reverse."

Khawaja's claim about the prevalence of ball tampering matches comments made by former Australian coach Darren Lehmann on ABC Sport's Summer Grandstand on Saturday.

Lehmann, who has joined the ABC's Cricket Podcast as co-host this season, said ball tampering had been a "big part of the game" until the Australians were caught in South Africa.

"You do know ball tampering is going on because it's been happening for 150 years," Lehmann said.

"I can only speak to what I know, and I know ball tampering was a big part of the game of cricket. Now it is obsolete.

Darren Lehmann stood down as Australian coach after Cape Town. (AP: Halden Krog)

"That doesn't make it right either, but that's the case, and we paid a heavy price for that."

Khawaja has been on the media trail promoting his book for the past two weeks, but the chapter about ball tampering had been redacted until Saturday morning.

The batter has been criticised for sitting on the information for eight years, however Khawaja defended the timing in a social media post while saying he felt he had not thrown anyone "under the bus" with his revelations.

Cricket Australia has continuously denied all players and staff knew about the South African ball tampering.

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Jennifer and Gretl Petelczyc were shot dead in their own home by Mark James Bombara. (ABC News)

A coronial inquest into the 2024 double murder of Perth mother Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl is due to begin today.

The inquest will focus on the medical care the killer, Mark Bombara, received ahead of the shooting.

The tragedy led to a toughening of Western Australia's gun laws, exposed police failings and put a spotlight on domestic violence.

A coronial inquest into the double murder of Perth mother Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl is expected to begin today, focusing on the medical care provided to their killer in the lead up to the fatal shooting.

WARNING: This story contains details that may distress some readers

Mark Bombara, 63, shot and killed his estranged wife's best friend, Jennifer Petelczyc, 59, and her daughter, Gretl, 18, in their Floreat home, before turning the gun on himself.

He had gone to their house in May 2024 looking for his estranged wife and his daughter.

Bombara made menacing phone calls, triggering a massive police response, but when officers arrived at the Berkeley Crescent home Bombara and Jennifer Petelczyc were dead.

Gretl was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital but died a short time later.

It was a tragedy that shocked the state, exposed police failings and forever changed the state's gun laws.

A pre-inquest hearing in June heard the coroner's primary focus would be investigating the medical care Bombara received in the lead-up to the shooting.

An expert neurological report on Bombara was requested, but no detail has been provided on Bombara's medical history or why the report was ordered.

The actions of police officers, the state's gun laws and how family and domestic violence played a role are also expected to be examined over five days.

Bombara's daughter, Ariel, had been trying to warn police for weeks that her father had a history of family and domestic violence and was a real and imminent threat.

Ariel Bombara says she repeatedly warned police about her father. (ABC News: Phil Hemingway)

She and her mother had fled the family home weeks earlier, fearing for their lives, and had told officers that one of Bombara's 13 guns was missing, but no action was taken.

A WA Police investigation found eight officers did not perform their duty and internal disciplinary action was taken.

No officer was sacked.

An internal investigation into the actions of WA Police officers in the weeks before Mark Bombara killed two women in the Perth suburb of Floreat finds eight officers did not perform their duty.

"The finding is that officers did not correctly assess the risk, therefore the available powers under the Restraining Orders Act and Firearms Act were not exercised appropriately," WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch said in January 2025.

Ariel Bombara's response to the police report was scathing.

"We told you he was going to murder us. So did you not believe us? Or did you just not give a sh*t?" she said at the time.

"This was the perfect storm of apathy and compassion fatigue from officers combined with shoddy systems, outdated policies and insufficient training and support that resulted in a lethal outcome."

The two women were slain in May 2024 at their home. (ABC News: Julian Robins)

One of the recommendations from the police report was for a family violence coordinator to always be present at the state Operations Command centre to allow officers to seek expert advice.

Australian Bureau of Statistics data shows WA Police are responding to one family and domestic violence incident every 20 minutes.

Mark Bombara legally owned 13 guns, including 11 firearms on a recreational licence and two handguns on a collector's licence.

That is no longer possible.

WA's gun laws are now among the toughest in the nation. (ABC News: Sam Clark)

Less than a week after the double-murder suicide, the WA Parliament vowed to change the state's gun laws.

The reforms came into effect in March 2025 and are now the toughest in the nation. They have reduced the number of licensed guns in the state by a quarter.

Recreational licences no longer exist, and collectors' licences are much stricter.

There are limits of 10 guns and a requirement for a mental health check every five years.

But what are likely to make the biggest difference are the disqualification orders, which allow for the immediate removal of a person's firearms when a report of domestic or family violence has been made.

The WA Labor government has put tackling family and domestic violence at the top of its agenda. In spite of this, eight police officers did not perform their duties in lead-up to the Floreat murders, according to an internal report.

It removes the ability for police officers to use discretion to assess whether the risk threshold has been met.

The changes were met with backlash from The Nationals and the WA Firearms Community Alliance who suggested they were an overreach affecting law-abiding gun owners, while not targeting illegal guns in the community.

A 2024 record-breaking ePetition in Parliament was signed by more than 31,000 people who also were against the changes.

The deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelczyc were a turning point for the state's response to domestic and family violence, but in the two years since, the number of women and children killed by violence has continued to climb.

According to Australian Femicide Watch, 60 women and 28 children across Australia have been killed by violence so far this year.

What more needs to be done to protect Australian families will be heard in the inquest, which is expected to sit for five days.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.title: Breaking: Nvidia investigates reports CEO had affair with Chinese spy
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Jensen Huang has admitted to the company's staff that he had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. (Reuters: Steve Marcus, file)

Technology giant Nvidia is launching an independent investigation after a media report that its CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Mr Huang admitted to staff he had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions.

The company says the investigation will be overseen by independent directors and legal counsel, but Mr Huang will remain in his role.

Technology giant and artificial chip manufacturer Nvidia says it is launching an independent investigation after a media report that its founder and CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Top Republican members of Congress in the US House of Representatives have called on Mr Huang to brief Congress this month about a New York Times report in October alleging he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

The media outlet reported last month that US authorities were investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia.

Jensen Huang has forged a close working relationship with US President Donald Trump amid the country's race to develop AI faster than China. (Reuters: Evan Vucci)

US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that were barred from shipment to China.

Nvidia said on Sunday, local time, that while its board had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information.

"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," a statement said.

"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."

Mr Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, the company said.

The founder of the world's most valuable AI company has the ear of Donald Trump when it comes to the risks and potential of the cutting-edge technology.

Axios reported on Sunday, citing a draft email by Mr Huang to employees, that he admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Mr Huang said in the draft email seen by Reuters.

Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, Mr Huang said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."

An Nvidia spokesperson said Mr Huang was "committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption."

Mr Huang is a central figure in the global push toward AI development, and has forced a close working relationship with United States President Donald Trump.

He has previously encouraged the White House to lift restrictions on the sale of advanced AI chips to China, arguing the measures accelerate Beijing's own development of the technology.

Jensen Huang has previously pushed for a relaxation of US restrictions against Nvidia in the interest of accelerating the global adoption of its technology.

Nvidia is valued at about $US5.4 trillion ($7.7 trillion), making it the world's most valuable company as demand for AI hardware and data centres has skyrocketed.

Mr Huang was born in Taiwan and raised in Thailand before he emigrated alone to the US to attend a boarding school at the age of 10.

He has previously described AI as the world's next industrial revolution and argues that whichever country has its technology adopted the most worldwide will win the AI race.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/k.title: Lawyers warn court fence plan could leave victims at risk from offenders
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/k.author: James Elton
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/k.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Court officials say the new fence is designed to prevent the building's windows being smashed after hours. (ABC News: James Elton)

Court officials want to construct a perimeter fence around the Katherine Courthouse to stop its windows being smashed.

However, domestic violence services say the fence could trap women in with their accused abusers in high-stress moments.

The NT Attorney-General's Department says design work is "ongoing" and feedback on how the fence could restrict movement is being considered.

Courthouse grounds in the Northern Territory town of Katherine could soon be surrounded by a "pool-style" perimeter fence, which court officials say is necessary to prevent windows being smashed after hours.

The proposed works also include a large rain tree in the garden at the front of the building being cut down as it has reportedly been dropping "sizeable" branches.

In a letter to court users obtained by the ABC, NT Local Court principal registrar Sarah Hannon said the fence was "required in response to a number of security and safety incidents at the courthouse, including incidents involving windows and doors being smashed".

The area has served as a place for lawyers to meet with their clients and for families to grieve during inquests. (ABC News: James Elton)

"We do not want the fencing to create an unnecessarily institutional or imposing appearance," Ms Hannon wrote.

"For that reason, we are proposing a relatively simple looped, pool-style fence rather than fencing with spikes or other more overt security features."

Unlike the NT's other major courthouses in Darwin and Alice Springs, where the buildings extend to the footpath, the Katherine courthouse has a large shady outdoor area with seating where witnesses, victims, accused people and families can wait for their case to be called.

The area has also served as an informal meeting place for lawyers to meet with their clients, and for family to grieve during coronial inquests.

The registrar's letter does not specify the height of the fence, but said the gate would be left open during the court's operating hours, allowing people to come and go freely.

Despite that assurance, the idea has been slammed by the Katherine Women's Information and Legal Service (KWILS).

The service's advocacy leader Brianna Bell said even with the gate open, the fence would create a bottleneck and reduce the number of viable escape routes should there be an incident within the court grounds.

Brianna Bell says victim-survivors could find themselves "in a confined space with someone who has wielded a weapon at you". (ABC News: James Elton)

"It really worries us to think about the number of victim-survivors that are attending court every single day who are experiencing things like threats or intimidation from the person who uses violence, or sometimes from their extended family," Ms Bell said.

Because court attendees only go through a metal detector once they enter the building itself, Ms Bell said it would be possible for someone armed with a knife to enter the fenced grounds undetected.

"You could be in a confined space with someone who has wielded a weapon at you and you can't just run in any direction, you need to run to the gate," she said.

The court has metal detectors to scan anyone entering the building but the fenced in area will not. (ABC News: James Elton)

"If they put themselves in front of where that gate is, you've got nowhere to go."

Ms Bell also questioned whether a non-spiked fence would actually work to prevent criminal damage occurring at night.

This is not the first time the design of the Katherine courthouse has come under criticism — earlier this year, sector experts called for urgent renovations to make the court safe for victim-survivors.

In response to questions from the ABC, a spokesperson for the NT Attorney-General's Department said the fence was intended to address "ongoing vandalism and property damage".

"Detailed design work is continuing, with stakeholder feedback on access, movement and safety being considered as part of the process," they said.

A large rain tree outside the court will be cut down as it has reportedly been dropping "sizeable" branches. (ABC News: James Elton)

The spokesperson also confirmed the works had been "initiated" by the administration of the NT Local Court and would be funded from within the court's existing budget.

Australia's domestic violence commissioner and local legal services have raised concerns about women's safety at Katherine Local Court, saying urgent upgrades are needed to protect victim-survivors.

KWILS said it was "disappointing" to see the court prioritise the fence and the removal of the tree, rather than investing in safety features like alternative entrances and exits.

A spokesperson for NT architecture firm Susan Dugdale and Associates said the company had submitted detailed plans for a major refurbishment of the Katherine courthouse to the NT government in December 2024.

They said the proposal came after the firm was commissioned to undertake the work by the previous Labor government, with the design focused on making the court safer and more welcoming for domestic violence victims.

In January, NT Attorney-General Marie-Clare Boothby said work on the refurbishment was ongoing.

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Domestic Violence

Police say Danielle Madgwick, 23, died after being stabbed multiple times by her partner. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Three more people have been charged in connection to the fatal stabbing of 23-year-old Danielle Madgwick in Wagga Wagga.

Ms Madgwick was found with multiple stab wounds to her upper body at a home in Kooringal on September 19.

She died at the scene despite efforts from paramedics.

A 31-year-old man, allegedly her partner, was arrested later that day and charged with domestic violence murder and remains before the courts.

A 31-year-old man has been charged over the fatal stabbing of a 23-year-old woman in Kooringal. (ABC News: Rachel Holdsworth)

Her death was one of multiple across New South Wales that weekend being investigated as a DV-related homicide.

The tragedy triggered investigations under Strike Force Ralore, where police executed a search warrant at a home in Wagga on Saturday.

The warrant prompted the arrest of two men, aged 18 and 56, and a 53-year-old woman on Saturday, who police allege were known to Ms Madgwick.

All three were charged with being accessories after the fact to domestic violence murder.

They were refused bail and are expected to appear in court again on December 23.

Counting Dead Women Australia, a register that tracks homicides of women, said 41 women have been killed so far in 2026.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/h.title: Break in SEQ storm activity as 'insufferable' heatwave lingers in Far North
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/h.author: Josh Dye
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/h.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

The BOM is warning residents in Far North Queensland to brace for another week of heatwave conditions.  (Supplied: BOM)

Parts of Queensland's Far North are sweltering through an extreme heatwave.

Weipa on the Cape York Peninsula had its hottest November day on record, during a 33-day streak of temperatures above 36C.

Severe storms have eased in the state's south-east, but are predicted to return from Wednesday.

Parts of Far North Queensland are enduring a record-breaking heatwave, as the south-east gets a short break from repeated thunderstorm activity.

The Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) said Weipa, on the Cape York Peninsula, had its hottest November day on record on Saturday, with the mercury tipping 39.8 degrees Celsius.

"Maximum temperatures have been really persisting in quite an exceptional heat around parts of the peninsula," meteorologist Kimba Wong said.

"We've now had 33 days in a row above 36 degrees for Weipa … That is insufferable heat.

Even Weipa's wildlife is struggling to stay cool, as this bird rests beside a garden sprinkler. (Supplied: Matthew Bright)

"Unfortunately, there's no end to the heat inside this week … that warm and unstable air mass isn't shifting anytime soon."

There is an extreme heatwave warning for the peninsula, while a severe heatwave warning is current for several other regions from the Gulf Country to the Whitsundays.

The BOM said parts of western Cape York Peninsula would have another week of maximum temperatures in the high 30s to low 40s, and overnight temperatures in the mid to high 20s.

Ominous skies in Point Vernon in Hervey Bay on Saturday. (ABC Wide Bay: Peta Johansen)

Localised heavy rainfall and storms are possible around Mackay and the Eungella ranges on Monday.

Ms Wong said south-east Queensland will see a brief reprieve from the storms peppering the region in the past week.

"Entering mid-November now it's in the midst of our storm season, so it wouldn't go a day without a thunderstorm somewhere in Queensland," she said.

"As we head into Tuesday, Wednesday [and] Thursday, the next trough system starts to push in across the state, so generally a little bit more unsettled weather returning to much of Queensland.

Beachgoers enjoy a Sunday morning swim at Miami on the Gold Coast.  (ABC Gold Coast: Dominic Cansdale)

"Perhaps a returning risk of some severe storms across south-east Queensland on Wednesday and Thursday."

Maximum temperatures are forecast to be milder in the south-east on Monday before ramping back up as the week progresses.

"The next slightly cooler change comes through later in the week," Ms Wong said.

Meanwhile, several flood warnings remain active for the state.

There are moderate warnings for flooding along the Barcoo, Bulloo and Upper Balonne rivers.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/p.title: Poland treats fatal mass shooting as 'terrorist offence'
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/p.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Unrest, Conflict and War

Scene of mass shooting in Poland’s Krakow

Polish prosecutors say a mass shooting that killed six people and injured at least 15 is being treated as an act "constituting a terrorist offence".

The square where the shooting occurred has reopened, with mourners gathering to lay flowers and candles.

Poland has entered two days of national mourning.

Polish prosecutors say a mass shooting that killed six people and injured at least 15 others is being treated as an act "constituting a terrorist offence".

The attack, which Poland's defence minister described as an "act of terror," happened on Saturday, local time, in the Main Square in the heart of Krakow's Old Town.

The square is a major tourist hub in the country's second-largest city.

Polish police guarded Krakow's Main Square more than a day after the shooting. (Reuters: Jakub Porzyck)

Four women and two men were killed in the shooting. Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, according to Malopolska regional governor Krzysztof Jan Klęczar.

A man from the United Kingdom and a woman from Austria were also among the dead, authorities said.

A video posted on social media showed a police officer repeatedly shooting the attacker, who was lying on the street. The officer later slowly collapsed to the ground.

Poland has entered two days of national mourning. (Reuters: Jakub Porzycki)

The two police officers who stopped the gunman, in actions authorities hailed as heroic, remain in hospital. They were both conscious by Sunday afternoon.

The bodies of the assailant's sister, mother and father were also found at the man's family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometres north-east of Krakow. They likely died from gunshot wounds.

The square reopened on Sunday evening, with mourners gathering to lay flowers and candles in honour of the victims.

Poland has entered two days of national mourning.

St. Mary's Trumpet Call, a traditional five-note melody which played every hour from the highest tower of St Mary's Basilica, was paused overnight — the first time the call had been missed since World War II.

Marie-Ange Collaer wrote on Facebook that she and her family survived the shooting during a trip to Krakow from Brussels.

"We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around," she wrote.

British resident Neil Thaxton and his wife also lived through the attack.

"We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots," he wrote on Facebook.

"We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off."

Witnesses who survived the shooting say they scrambled to find refuge in nearby stores. (Reuters: Jakub Porzycki)

Alexandros Maronitis, a tourist from Greece, told The Associated Press that he could not get back to his lodgings for five hours after the shooting.

"We saw the shooter when they picked him up with the ambulance," he said.

"So, we're a bit afraid. It's our first time in Poland. We heard it's a safe country."

Krakow's St Anne's Church was packed with people who attended a memorial service. (AP: Jakub Porzycki)

Witness Andy Hill told the BBC he felt as though he was in a movie scene.

"It doesn't feel real," he said.

"And the trouble is, you have such an instantaneous moment to make a decision: Run. Stand still. There's an element of shock. But I just thought the easiest thing to do is dive through a doorway and just take refuge behind the windows."

Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect held "very radical" and "ultranationalistic" views.

"Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies," he said at a news conference on Saturday.

Four women and two men are dead, 15 others are injured and the gunman is in hospital after a shooting in a market square in the Polish city of Krakow.

Local officials in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski said they seized seven weapons from the family home, bringing the total number recovered to 11, including four found on the suspect or in his car in Krakow.

Both father and son had gun permits, they said.

The suspect, a Polish citizen, remains in a critical condition after undergoing multiple surgeries.

There was confusion on Saturday about his age, with authorities first saying 24 and later 25. On Sunday they confirmed he was 24.

The suspect's dead sibling was a young artist studying at the Krakow Academy of Fine Arts.

"Nothing will ever be like before. The delicate tissue of our academic community was painfully wounded," the academy wrote in a statement on Sunday.

A shooting club in Starachowice, where the suspect is believed to have trained, said it only offered "static shooting". (Reuters: Kacper Pempel)

The academy confirmed Magdalena Oksińska was a third year student and that, additionally, the sister of an academy employee was shot twice.

"Magdalena Oksińska, 21 years old, a queer person, was an absolutely talented painter, photographer, poet and writer," architect Pavko Krajka wrote in a post on social media, accompanied by images of the artist's colourful paintings.

About 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.

The Swit shooting club in Starachowice, where the suspect is believed to have trained, issued a statement on Sunday saying it offered only "static shooting," which involves firing from a fixed position at a stationary target.

The club said the suspect "was never trained in our club in the areas of dynamic, tactical or combat shooting".

Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland, however, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many injured, including children.

The Krakow shooter's military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other "extreme right lone actors" committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague.

"We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland," he said.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.title: Inmate complaints surge 60 per cent amid lockdowns and device shortages
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.author: Toby Hemmings
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Inmate complaints in NSW have surged to more than 32,000 in the past year. (AAP: Jono Searle)

The latest annual report from the NSW Inspector of Custodial Services reveals inmate complaints rose 60 per cent in 2025-26 to 32,168.

Corrective Services NSW says the rise in complaints is "not necessarily an indicator of worsening conditions".

Greens justice spokesperson Sue Higginson cites a number of factors, including the increase in prisoners on remand.

Inmate complaints about NSW prisons have skyrocketed in the past year, according to the latest annual report by the state's prisons inspector.

Official Visitors to NSW prisons reported 32,168 complaints in the year to June 30, 2026, a 60 per cent increase on the previous year.

The surge in complaints to independent authorities comes as the state's prison population continues to rise, driven by more people being refused bail and held on remand.

Corrections Minister Anoulack Chanthivong declined an interview, but a Corrective Services NSW (CSNSW) spokeswoman said that "an increase in complaints is not necessarily an indicator of worsening conditions".

"It can also reflect a larger inmate population, [an] increase in visits from Official Visitors and confidence in the independent processes available to raise concerns and seek assistance," she said.

University of Technology Sydney law professor Thalia Anthony said the figures left her "completely astonished … because the rate of complaints far exceeds the increase in people in prison".

"There are grounds for people in prison to feel that their conditions are worsening, but I didn't expect this level of escalation of complaints," she said.

Professor Thalia Anthony says the number of new inmates is outstripping the number of prison staff.  (ABC News: Jack Ailwood)

Prisoner complaints are made in person to Official Visitors, who are independent community representatives appointed by the corrections minister.

There are 93 Official Visitors appointed to examine conditions in adult and youth justice centres, take enquiries and complaints, and submit reports to the NSW government.

In 2025-26, medical issues were the most complained about topic.

Complaints about unfair treatment, tablet computers and correctional centre routine surged over the past year, with the annual report stating that one of the biggest sources of complaint was lock-ins or lockdowns.

"Short staffing and the subsequent impact of inmate lock-ins have been further compounded by the limited availability of functioning tablets and the cost of phone calls," the report stated.

Greens justice spokesperson Sue Higginson said she believed an additional factor in the "explosion" in complaints was a 2025 law change to lower the standard of proof when disciplining inmates.

"We know that inmates were being accused of things they hadn't done and then being really punished," she said.

"The complaint system is where these grievances ultimately end up."

Sue Higginson says the complaints are a result of a populist tough-on-crime approach. (Supplied: Sue Higginson)

Ms Higginson said the rise was indicative of the "populist law and order approach" from the Minns government.

"You see an increased prison population in centres that are not fit for purpose; of course the complaints are going to rise," she said.

The report stated "the vast majority of complaints … were resolved at the centre level," with only a small number referred to the Commissioner of CSNSW.

A CSNSW spokeswoman said that Official Visitors fulfilled an "important function to ensure our correctional system remains open, fair, and transparent".

Remand populations have risen significantly, following the tightening of bail laws for those accused of serious domestic violence offences.

According to the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Applied Research (BOCSAR), in the three years to 2026, there has been a 32 per cent increase in prisoners held on remand.

Remand populations in NSW prisons have risen significantly over the past three years. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

Public Service Association NSW general secretary Stewart Little estimated there were around 7,000 people currently held on remand in a prison population of approximately 14,200.

"It means that there's a lot of pressure whenever you've got a large number of remandees coming into the system," he said.

"Often they're affected by drug or alcohol or other substance abuse; they require legal visits and they require a lot of assistance."

In September, the government announced it would reopen the mothballed Dawn de Loas Correctional Centre at Silverwater and fast-track adding extra beds at Parklea Correctional Centre to meet the growing population.

The de-privatisation of Parklea Correctional Centre has been fast-tracked to add extra beds to the corrections system. (ABC News: Nick Dole)

But Professor Anthony said without hiring more staff, the prison system would be remain strained.

"I think it's incumbent on the Minns government to look at these rising complaints and ask whether prison is the right place for these people," she said.

"By providing inhumane conditions, by mistreating people in prison, we are setting them up to return to the community more disgruntled, more disengaged with the system and institutions.

"That's not going to lead to greater safety."

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/v.title: What to expect from Victoria's construction corruption royal commission
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/v.author: Judd Boaz
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/v.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Royal Commissions

The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria will have its first public hearing today. (ABC News: Patrick Rocca)

The Victorian government's Big Build is a multi-decade, $100 billion construction project comprising new roads, railway stations and tunnels.

But major infrastructure project construction sites have become hotbeds for allegations of criminal wrongdoing, corruption and serious misconduct.

The Victorian government has called a royal commission into the alleged corruption, with its first hearings to begin this week.

Here's what you need to know about the Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria.

Allegations of corruption and the criminal infiltration of the CFMEU construction union and Victoria's Big Build were first aired by Nine newspapers in 2024.

Among the allegations were claims that bikies and criminals acting as union delegates had received hundreds of thousands of dollars working on federal and state government funded projects.

The reporting led to the federal government placing parts of the union into administration in August 2024.

The Victorian branch of the CFMEU will be at the centre of investigations by the royal commission. (AAP: Joel Carrett)

Following this, the union's administrators tasked Geoffrey Watson SC to report on the way the CFMEU was operating under former union boss John Setka.

Mr Watson found the union in Victoria had "collapsed into a squalid mess" and suggested Victorian taxpayers had lost as much as $15 billion to organised crime on Big Build projects.

He found the Victorian construction division of the CFMEU began controlling which subcontractors and labour hire companies were allowed on major construction sites.

In Victoria, he found widespread corruption "of a very organised kind, which involved not only financial crimes against the people of Victoria in terms of what was going on there, but also sites being used as drug dealing points".

Former chief justice of South Australia Chris Kourakis was appointed Commissioner. (ABC News: Lincoln Rothall)

Despite the report, the Victorian government was slow to call a royal commission to investigate the claims.

The topic of a royal commission seemingly split the Victorian government earlier this year, with former premier Jacinta Allan steadfastly refusing to call one despite growing calls from across the political spectrum.

Her ousting as leader and the ascension of Ben Carroll to the top job marked a major shift, with the new premier immediately calling for a royal commission within hours of his election.

Ben Carroll's first act as Victorian premier was to call the royal commission. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

The terms of reference define the key areas of investigation that a royal commission must examine, as well as the timeline it must do so in.

This royal commission will inquire into:

The first block of public hearings begins on November 9 and runs until November 20.

The hearings are open to the public and will be held on Level 9, 54 Wellington Street in Collingwood, with a usual start time of 10am.

The hearings will also be livestreamed for those who cannot attend in person.

A second block of hearings will be held before the end of the year, with the royal commission to continue its work through the November 28 state election.

The commission has already held some closed hearings, where sensitive information that will shape the investigation was aired.

A range of witnesses from across the construction industry and government will be called during the first round of hearings.

While the list has not been made public yet, we can expect CFMEU members, public servants at the Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (VIDA), ministerial staff and workers at major contracting companies involved with Big Build projects, to be called.

There is a chance former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan will be called to give evidence.

Former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan could be called as witnesses.  (AAP Image: Daniel Pockett)

In August, premier Ben Carroll said "anyone and everyone can be called" and that it would be up to the commissioner to determine who and what was relevant to its inquiries, including former premiers.

"If he wants to hear from ministers, former ministers, senior officials, union leaders or company executives, he has the power to call them," he said.

At the time, CFMEU administrator Michael Crosby said "developers, head contractors, subcontractors, labour hire operators and anyone else who had profited from unlawful or unethical behaviour" should be called "if this royal commission is serious about uncovering the truth".
