https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS
https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.text:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.

As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

Funded by cash reallocated from existing GP budgets for 2026-27, the scheme will allow surgeries to identify and provide extra care to the patients they believe are most at risk of becoming seriously unwell in the winter. Groups of GP practices can use £126 for every eligible patient supported.

The prime minister said the scheme would be targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty and lung conditions such as emphysema and other types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Andy Burnham said he was “not going to pretend this winter will be easy” but the programme would help keep people well at home and avoid unnecessary trips to hospital.

“If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E,” he said.

“People deserve the right care in the right place. And our NHS staff, who work so hard, deserve the right tools to provide it. I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.”

The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said the scheme had been designed to offer greater support to the frailest patients.

“After such a heavy summer for our NHS as a result of the heat, everyone is working together to prepare for more challenging winter pressures,” she said. “That includes the rollout of flu vaccinations, investing in extra urgent care capacity and strengthening partnerships with social care.

“With thousands more GPs in post and millions more GP appointments this year, the £40m programme to support vulnerable patients in the community is part of our plan to help patients, improve primary care and also to support our NHS through the heavier winter months.”

Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, the president of the Royal College of GPs, said she welcomed the focus on prevention and supporting patients at greatest risk of avoidable hospital admission this winter.

“GPs’ clinical expertise, knowledge of their patients and continuity of care are central to identifying those most in need and providing personalised, coordinated support,” she said.

But she also said short-term initiatives alone could not deliver “sustained improvements in care” that patients with complex health needs required. Instead, she said, a longer-term approach to prevention was necessary, which must be backed by “sustainable investment in general practice”.
https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.summary: £40m scheme aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays. Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England to receive extra support from their GP. Scheme will allow surgeries to identify and provide extra care to patients they believe are most at risk of becoming seriously unwell in the winter.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: President Milei welcomes Pope Leo during historic visit to Argentina
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Argentinian President Javier Milei has welcomed the head of the Catholic Church, Pope Leo XIV, upon his arrival at Jorge Newbery airport near Buenos Aires.

Milei and his sister, presidential secretary Karina Milei, greeted the pope on Sunday amid tensions between the government and Argentina’s Catholic Church over austerity measures.

Prior to his arrival, the pope spent three days in Uruguay, the first stop on his tour of Latin America.

He is the first pontiff to visit Argentina in nearly four decades, since John Paul II’s trip in 1987.

“Without a doubt, it gives us great joy that this pope is visiting us,” said Jorge Silanes, religious director at the Pequeno Cottolengo Don Orione, a home for people with disabilities in the Buenos Aires province.

In Argentina, Pope Leo’s schedule includes attending a welcome ceremony at Plaza San Martin and a meeting with Milei at the Casa Rosada, the official presidential palace.

But the pontiff’s visit comes amid shrinking membership in the Catholic Church in Latin America, as well as a sometimes fractious relationship with politicians like Milei.

Catholics comprise the largest religious group in Latin America, with as many as 425 million people identifying with the church.

But their numbers have shrunk over the last decade. A Pew Research Center survey found that, in Argentina, the percentage of self-identifying Catholics slipped from 71 percent in the 2013-2014 year to 58 percent a decade later.

Milei himself has suggested he considered converting to Judaism, though he was raised in the Catholic faith.

The Catholic Church has also criticised Milei’s austerity measures, which included slashing social spending and safety-net programmes for the poor.

Milei has defended the budget cuts as necessary to bring inflation under control.

Some members of the Catholic clergy, however, have taken a visible role in the protests against Milei’s measures.

Leo, 71, the first US-born pope, will remain in Argentina until Wednesday and meet with officials, diplomats and civil society representatives.

He will also visit a prison and celebrate mass in Buenos Aires, Lujan, and the province of Cordoba, before travelling to Peru, where he spent years serving as a bishop.

The previous pope, Francis, was born in Buenos Aires in 1936 and was the first pope from the Americas, but he never visited his home country as head of the Catholic Church. Francis died in 2025.

He and Milei had a notably contentious relationship, with the Argentinian president calling the late pontiff a “communist” and an “imbecile who defends social justice”.

“Leo is going to make the visit that Francis never did,” said Reverend Lorenzo “Toto” de Vedia, who works with poor communities in a neighbourhood of Buenos Aires.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.summary: Pope Leo XIV is the first pontiff to visit Argentina in nearly four decades. He is the head of the Catholic Church in Latin America. The pope has been criticised by the Catholic church over austerity measures.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: US chipmaker Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence.

In an announcement on Sunday, Nvidia said the probe would be conducted by a “committee of independent directors” with outside counsel.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said.

It said the board continued to have “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team”. Huang will continue to lead Nvidia during the probe.

The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot.

China and the US have been in competition to dominate key tech sectors like artificial intelligence (AI).

Amid the AI boom, Nvidia has seen demand for its chips and programming interfaces explode, resulting in the company being valued in the trillions of dollars.

For years, the US has sought to restrict the export of advanced chips to China, fearing the Asian superpower could gain an edge over its technology and military sectors.

But on October 29, The New York Times said it had obtained exclusive information that a Chinese woman named Alice Huang, or Huang Le, sought to cultivate close ties with Jensen Huang in an effort to glean information about Nvidia’s technology.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, has denied any allegations of spying in the case.

The New York Times also reported that Alice Huang’s employer, Megaspeed, had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing some $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.

Jensen Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, who is of no relation, spurred fierce bipartisan backlash in the US Congress in the aftermath of the report.

“For months, bipartisan members of Congress have raised concerns about NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips going to China,” Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote in a statement.

“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China.”

Republican lawmakers in the House of Representatives also called on Huang to appear and testify before Congress about the affair on November 18.

“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republicans John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.

In an email to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Huang had admitted to having an extramarital relationship.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse ‌for what I did,” Huang said.

Nvidia has grown rapidly in recent years with the rise of AI, producing chips for large language models developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google.

Huang has also been closely working with US President Donald Trump since the Republican leader returned to office in 2025.

In August of that year, the Trump administration announced it would take a 15 percent cut of certain Nvidia chip sales to China.

Trump reportedly bought as much as $1.6m in Nvidia stock and sold about $1m in August, ahead of November’s midterm elections.

After the midterm races last Tuesday, stocks for AI-related companies, including Nvidia, tumbled in reaction to widespread Republican losses.

Trump has pushed back against calls to regulate AI companies, but many Democrats during the midterms campaigned on placing restrictions on the companies, including on the construction of data centres.

Nvidia lost $450bn in market value in a single trading day last week, but it rebounded on Friday, regaining 4 percent of its losses.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence. The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, has denied any allegations of spying in the case.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: Why Trump wants UFC chief Dana White as his new White House press secretary
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.author: Umar Farooq
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday to discuss taking the job of White House press secretary.

Trump announced the offer on Saturday, days after his Republican Party suffered record losses in midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, the president praised White as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” who would bring along leading UFC fighters as “assistants” to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.

But it remains unclear how serious the offer is. In a news conference on Saturday, White confirmed he would travel to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump. But he also signalled concerns about his existing workload.

“I got a lot of jobs already,” White, a Trump ally and donor, said. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”

White also posted a photo to Instagram Stories of himself standing behind the White House podium. Its caption read, “On to the next chapter.”

Trump, too, posted his own AI-generated memes about the potential hire.

On Sunday, he shared an animated cartoon of White in the White House briefing room, flanked by a row of fighters. One of them body-slams a reporter who asks, “Is Trump a threat to democracy?”

The press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure ended ‌last ⁠month. She left the post within five days of being hired after facing criticism that she presented herself as a lawyer without being licensed in the US.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August, citing the needs of her growing family.

But why is the head of a mixed martial arts franchise being considered for the new public face of the Trump administration? Al Jazeera explains that and more in this brief explainer.

A former bouncer and small-time boxer, White began his career as a businessman by opening a boxing gym in Boston where he trained other fighters.

He later moved to Las Vegas, where he continued to run gyms and manage emerging fighters.

The UFC was founded in 1993, at about the time White resettled in Las Vegas. The organisation sought to offer an arena for fighters from different disciplines – from boxing to wrestling to jujitsu – to face each other in “no-holds-barred” competition.

In 2001, White convinced two casino magnate friends to buy the UFC for $2m and name him president. Since then, he has built the company up through big fights and lucrative pay-per-view television deals.

He has been a fixture in the UFC in the more than two decades since. White has been credited with turning the fledgling franchise into a global business that brought mixed martial arts into the mainstream.

In 2016, the UFC was sold for $4bn, and in 2023, White became its CEO after a merger with World Wrestling Entertainment valued at some $21bn.

White has been a longtime supporter of Trump, appearing by his side at campaign events for nearly a decade.

Trump, in turn, has a history of hosting UFC fights as far back as 2001. At the time, UFC was struggling against criticism that the sport was too violent.

White had just taken up his position as UFC president, and he and Trump came to an agreement to host that year’s UFC championship at Trump’s Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

The next year, the UFC returned to the Taj Mahal.

Speaking in support of Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention, White recalled how the early collaboration helped open doors for the UFC, making other venues more accessible.

“No arenas wanted us,” White said at the time. “This guy reached out, and he’s always been a friend to me.”

The 2016 election cycle would mark Trump’s first successful bid for public office. In 2018, White was invited to visit the White House during Trump’s inaugural term as president.

During the 2020 elections, White again endorsed Trump as he sought a second term as president. White also donated $1m to Trump’s campaign and was a key speaker at the Republican Party’s national convention that year.

“I’ve known this man for 20 years. We’ve actually become even closer since he’s become the president of the United States,” White told supporters at a rally in Colorado. “He’s a fighter. He loves this country. He’s doing great things for this country, and we’ve got to win this election again.”

Trump lost the 2020 race to Democrat Joe Biden. But four years later, in 2024, he launched another re-election bid, and successfully won a second term.

During that campaign, Trump credited White with helping him connect with younger voters.

“He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,” Trump told Time Magazine in May. “I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I’m saying, ‘Where the hell did you meet these people?’ They’re called influencers.”

Experts say Trump’s 2024 campaign benefitted significantly from his UFC connections.

Ahead of his victory, Trump courted influencers like UFC fan Theo Von and UFC host Joe Rogan, whose podcast boasts about 11 million listeners per episode.

Trump has also used his second term as president to elevate the UFC’s profile, weaving one of its events into plans to celebrate the 250th US Independence Day.

Dubbed “UFC Freedom 250”, the tournament was given unusual access to national monuments for a commercial event.

White, for instance, hosted a weigh-in for fighters on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, with uniformed military personnel standing as an honour guard. The fights themselves were held on the lawn of the White House.

Trump called the event “one of the most exciting days in the history of our fabled White House”.

But critics warned the event could constitute a conflict of interest: In the months before the fight, Trump reportedly bought up to $50,000 of stock in TKO Holding, the UFC’s parent company.

A lawsuit also challenged the UFC’s use of public facilities, calling the event “deeply corrupt”.

Some opposition figures have dismissed Trump’s idea of appointing White as press secretary as a way to distract attention from the midterm elections.

During the November 3 elections, Trump’s Republican Party suffered record losses, losing majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Melat Kiros, a Democrat elected to represent Colorado in the House, said on Saturday that Trump’s offer to White “demonstrates how deeply unserious this man is, how ridiculous this administration is”.

Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, meanwhile, said Trump’s choice raised questions about the president’s wellbeing.

“It would be really funny if it wasn’t dangerous, if he wasn’t the president,” Kelly said. “Countries around the world are continuing to laugh at us because of what he’s doing.”

There has also been some speculation that Trump may have tapped the wrong Dana White.

A woman by the same name formerly worked as a Pentagon spokesperson during Trump’s first term. She has denied being approached for the press secretary role.

“To everyone texting me congratulations: thank you, but you have the wrong Dana White,” she wrote on LinkedIn.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/08/apps-t.title: Apps to distract you from the endless cycle of doomscrolling
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/08/apps-t.author: Aisha Malik
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/08/apps-t.text:
You open your phone to check the time or a quick message. The next thing you know, an hour has passed and you’ve scrolled through endless celebrity drama, cat videos, awful news stories, influencer rants, and whatever else the algorithm decided to throw at you.

Even though you probably don’t want to keep wasting your time and energy on this mind-numbing content, you do it again the next day.

Doomscrolling, the habit of spending excessive amounts of time consuming content on social media, has become incredibly widespread. A survey from last year found that 64% of Americans say they doomscroll.

Researchers have warned that doomscrolling can negatively affect several aspects of your well-being, including your mental health and attention span. Spending long periods scrolling can lead to brain fatigue, difficulty focusing, and disrupted sleep. And if a lot of the content you’re consuming is negative or stressful, it can leave you feeling disheartened, anxious, and emotionally drained.

It’s hard to break the cycle of doomscrolling, but there are plenty of apps that provide content that’s engaging and productive.

Of course, you could always read a book or go for a walk (we have a guide on how to stop doomscrolling), but this list is for when you have a few spare minutes and want something to do on your phone that isn’t endless scrolling.

Finch is a self-care pet app that’s designed to help you build healthy habits. You care for a cute virtual pet by completing small daily goals, such as drinking enough water, going on a walk, and practicing mindfulness. You can write about your day, complete a breathing exercise, or send good vibes to a friend by adding them to the app.

The more self-care you do, the more your pet thrives. The app offers a fun way to trade mindless scrolling for small moments of self-care.

Finch is available for free on iOS and Android.

Libby is a free reading app that connects you to your local public library’s digital collection of ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines. All you need is a library card to borrow thousands of titles, which makes it easy to turn screen time into something productive.

You can explore a new book during a commute or while waiting at a doctor’s office, turning moments when your fingers might otherwise itch to scroll into opportunities to read.

Libby is available for free on iOS and Android.

If you want to take a break from doomscrolling and try something creative, Dudel Draw might be a good app for you. Each day, the app gives you a random shape that you turn into a drawing. These daily shapes vary from basic geometrical forms to more complex and abstract designs.

You can also get your friends in on the creativity with some fun competition by comparing your different creations, which could provide a nice break from sending each other endless TikToks or Instagram Reels.

Dudel Draw is available for free on iOS.

If you still want to feel connected to the world without scrolling through social media, you can check out Radio Garden. The app lets you listen to over 25,000 live radio stations from across the globe.

Once you open the app, you’ll see green dots marking cities and towns. Tap any dot to listen to radio stations broadcasting from that location. You can add favorites or search for radio stations, countries, and places.

Radio Garden is free, but it also offers an ad-free premium plan for $2.99 per month. The app is available on both iOS and Android.

Elevate is an app designed to help improve focus, memory, reading, math skills, and other cognitive abilities. It includes over 40 games to train different abilities you use in everyday life, from reading faster to comparing prices more efficiently.

You can track training streaks and compare your mind’s performance over time.

The app offers a free version with access to three games per day, or a yearly subscription of $39.99 for unlimited access. It’s available on both iOS and Android.

Vocabulary is an app that helps you learn new words every day. You can pick your difficulty level and choose categories that interest you, like emotions, the human body, business, and more. Each word comes with a definition, example sentences, and a guide on how to pronounce it.

The app also includes mini-games to help you review the words you’ve learned. You can set a goal of how many words you want to learn each week and create a regular learning routine.

Vocabulary offers a free trial, and then costs $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year. It’s available on iOS and Android.

If you’re a geography nerd looking to test your knowledge or just want to improve your geography skills, Seterra is perfect for you. The app features over 300 different games to test your map skills. You can test your knowledge of world flags; discover oceans, seas, and rivers; and explore mountain ranges and volcanoes across the globe.

Seterra lets you track your progress across categories and see leaderboards for top scorers for each game.

The app is free and available on both iOS and Android.

The NYT Games app offers several word, logic, and number games that change every day to exercise your mind. You can play the crossword, try the word-guessing game Wordle, group words with a common theme in Connections, see how many words you can make from seven letters in Spelling Bee, and more.

The app costs $5.99 per month for unlimited access and archives, but some games like Wordle, Strands, and the Mini Crossword are available to play for free.

NYT Games is available on both iOS and Android.

If you want to learn a new language but want to try something other than Duolingo, Drops is a good option. The app uses visually engaging mini‑games to help you build vocabulary and common phrases in more than 45 languages, with bite‑sized lessons designed to be completed in about five minutes a day.

Drops is designed for both beginners and experts who want to grow their foreign language vocabulary.

The free version of the app offers five-minute lessons per day. You can get unlimited access and premium features for $11.99 per month or $79.99 per year. The app is available on both iOS and Android.

Diaspora Problems is one of the 21st century’s best punk albums.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Diaspora Problems is one of the 21st century’s best punk albums.

Soul Glo has a new record called NA I’M GON GRAB ALLAT coming out in January, and I, for one, can not wait. While two singles have dropped, it’s not enough to truly tide me over, so I’ve been revisiting Songs to Yeet at the Sun and my favorite album of 2022 — Diaspora Problems.

“Gold Chain Punk (whogonbeatmyass?)” is an opening salvo for the ages. Bong rip, into a catchy-as-hell hardcore riff, with frontman Pierce Jordan ranting. Then comes the half-time stomp as Jordan gets fully unhinged, screaming “Who gon beat my ass? Who the fuck gon beat my ass?” From here on out, as the music shifts through a few different sections, the energy never comes down. Jordan shreds his vocal cords, begging, “Can I live?” Before finally spelling it out for anyone still confused:

Say more, say less, it’s all the same
When it’s time to die we can meet outside
To see who gon feel my pain

The record barely lets up from here on out. “Coming Correct” opens with a cough and a steady 808, giving you literally three seconds to catch your breath before Jordan jumps on the mic shouting, “I try to listen the way, I wanna be listened to.” The song starts stacking elements quickly, reaching full firestorm by 25 seconds in, and then does let up for the rest of its three-minute runtime.

The front chunk of the record is just perfect unrelenting hardcore song after perfect unrelenting hardcore song. Jordan’s crazed charisma is undeniable as he ricochets between leftist rhetoric, goofy bits about smoking weed, and vulnerable explorations of his struggles with depression. You’d be forgiven for struggling to keep up with his rapid-fire delivery, which owes almost as much to modern rappers as it does to classic hardcore acts like Minor Threat or Bad Brains.

Track six, “Driponomics,” fully embraces those more modern influences with trap snares, wall-rattling 808 kicks, and a guest verse from Mother Maryrose. The sampled guitar calls to mind the sax squeals favored by the Bomb Squad… just heavier.

The album eventually culminates in “Spiritual Level Of Gang Shit,” which features guest verses from McKinley Dixon and Lojii over gently echoed guitar melodies and dub-inspired groove. Then, around the 2:20 mark, things take a turn as the guitars turn punishing and the drums shift to a standard hardcore beat. But the song hasn’t reached its final form yet. That comes almost a minute later when the horn section kicks in.

Next to other modern hardcore standard bearers like Turnstile, Soul Glo might almost seem like traditionalists heavily influenced by the DC scene. But Diaspora Problems shows their ambition and willingness to take risks. Soul Glo plays with genre, is confrontational in its politics, and is generally just uncompromising.

Oh, and they put on a hell of a live show (I’ve seen them at least four times now). Don’t miss their incredible Tiny Desk Concert either, which I’m pretty sure is the first mosh pit to even open up in the NPR offices.

Soul Glo’s Diaspora Problems is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including Qobuz, Deezer, YouTube Music, Apple Music, and Spotify.

https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/08/sudd.title: Survival after sudden cardiac arrest didn’t improve despite training bystanders, emergency responders
https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/08/sudd.author: Elizabeth Cooney
https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/08/sudd.text:
CHICAGO — Sudden cardiac arrest statistics are chilling. In the United States, 350,000 people’s heartbeats, breathing, pulse, and blood circulation will all halt outside hospitals this year, seemingly out of the blue. These are not heart attacks. Only 1 in 10 people will survive them.

CPR and defibrillation can save their lives (and brains), but that depends on bystanders and emergency response systems being both nearby and prepared to step in — immediately. Survival chances drop by 10% for every minute that goes by without CPR.

Hints from observational studies suggested better, more comprehensive community training can help, which means educating 911 dispatchers, first responders, and potential bystanders. But results from a randomized controlled trial presented Sunday at the American Heart Association’s scientific sessions and published in the New England Journal of Medicine on Sunday show that approach has not worked, or at least not yet. But examples in Denmark may point the way forward.

By Elizabeth Cooney and Matthew Herper

By Casey Ross and Brittany Trang

https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.title: Left bundle branch pacing superior for atrioventricular block
https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.author: Scott Buzby
https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.text:
Purpose-built for physicians

CHICAGO — Left bundle branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing for reducing all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization and pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in patients with atrioventricular block.

These findings support left bundle branch (LBB) pacing as a first-line pacing strategy for patients needing high ventricular pacing, according to the OptimPacing researchers. The study was presented at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

“Right ventricular pacing is traditional pacing for heart block, but it’s associated with left ventricular dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction, increasing pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, heart failure and mortality. However, left bundle branch pacing is a novel physiological pacing. It can preserve the left ventricular synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing remain uncertain,” Jiangang Zou, MD, PhD, professor of cardiology at First Affiliated Hospital, Nanjing Medical University in China, said during a press conference. “We hypothesized that LBB pacing is superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, heart failure and mortality.”

OptimPacing was an investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized trial. Researchers enrolled 702 patients with an indication for permanent pacemaker implantation with high ventricular pacing burden, LV ejection fraction greater than 35% and NYHA functional class I to III. Patients were randomly assigned to LBB pacing or RV pacing, of whom 685 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 68 years; 58% men).

The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, HF hospitalization or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.

The researchers planned an interim analysis when at least 50 primary outcome events had occurred, after which the trial could be terminated early if the P value was less than .003, according to the study methods. The interim analysis was performed at a median follow-up of 35.1 months after 51 primary outcome events occurred. The researchers terminated the trial early for superiority of LBB pacing.

At the time of the interim analysis, 16 patients assigned to LBB pacing experienced a primary outcome event vs. 35 patients in the RV pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% vs. 19.2%; HR = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.23-0.75; P by stratified log-rank test = .003), according to the results.

Respective of each component of the primary composite outcome:

The researchers reported that LV end-diastolic volume and LV end-systolic volume were lower in the LBB pacing group and LVEF was higher than the RV pacing group.

Pacing parameters including R-wave sensing, impedance and threshold were stable in both groups, and LBB capture threshold remained low and stable, according to the presentation.

“LBB pacing demonstrates superiority over right ventricular pacing in preserving cardiac function and reducing pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and heart failure hospitalization,” Zou said during the presentation. “This study provides evidence supporting the consideration of LBB pacing as the first-line pacing strategy for patients with high ventricular pacing requirement.”

After the presentation, Elaine Wan, MD, the Esther Aboodi Associate Professor of Medicine in Cardiology and Cardiac Electrophysiology at Columbia University Medical Center, discussed the results of OptimPacing and what they could mean for future clinical guidelines.

“What we’ve learned here from this clinical trial, as we’ve learned when we buy a car or buy a house, is that location, location, location is very important. Here we’re showing that more physiological pacing instead of the traditional right ventricular pacing has shown benefit for physiological pacing,” Wan said. “There is definitely a reduction in pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, zero, over their median of 35.1 months follow-up, and there was a reduction in all-cause death, hospitalization, and over the 35 months, the function of the device showed stable threshold sensing and impedance.

“Is it time for a guideline change? As we can see from the guidelines from 2023 [Heart Rhythm Society and Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society and Latin American Heart Rhythm Society], currently, the guideline is that ventricular pacing for patients who require high pacing burden it is a class II a [recommendation]. I look forward to manuscript reviews from the community and also forthcoming larger trials to show whether or not conduction system pacing through left bundle pacing is the future in [cardiac electrophysiology].”

Zou J, et al. LBS.04. Late-breaking science: Innovations to optimize arrhythmia care. Presented at: American Heart Association Scientific Sessions; Nov. 6-9, 2026; Chicago.

Disclosures: Wan reports consulting for Boston Scientific. Zou reports no relevant financial disclosures.

https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-j.title: Read Huang's email to his staff and statement from Nvidia's board of directors
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-j.author: Terri Cullen
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-j.text:
Nvidia
 on Sunday said it has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies said is a Chinese spy.

“Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” the company told CNBC in a statement.

Below is a staff email from Huang obtained by CNBC and a statement released Sunday about the investigation from Nvidia’s board of directors.

[From:] Jensen Huang
[To:] Employees

Subj.: A message to our company

To my colleagues at NVIDIA,

I owe my family and all of you an apology.

I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.

Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.

To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.

To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.

Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.

My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.

— Jensen

The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.

While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.

Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

https://thehill.com/homenews/house/62057.author: Sudiksha Kochi
https://thehill.com/homenews/house/62057.text:
Congress returns to Capitol Hill after the astonishing midterm elections that dealt Republicans major losses and left Democrats riding high. Now, Republicans face their next major test: a fight over who will lead the party in the House as it prepares its descent into the minority.

House Republicans are scheduled to hold their leadership elections Nov. 10. Speaker Mike Johnson (La.) told lawmakers on a staff call last week that he will not run for minority leader, setting the stage for a potentially bruising contest between House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (La.) and House Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan (Ohio).

Republican Whip Tom Emmer (Minn.) and GOP Conference Chair Lisa McClain (Mich.) are both seeking to retain their leadership positions in the minority. But neither is guaranteed a smooth path, with both facing challengers from within the conference.

Johnson has more than a leadership transition to contend with during the final weeks of the congressional session.

Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) will reintroduce articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week, largely over his handling of the war in Iran. Several Republicans, including Vice President Vance, have pointed to the conflict as a reason for the party’s election losses, though they have stopped short of calling for Hegseth’s ouster.

Congress also faces a looming Dec. 11 government funding deadline. Lawmakers must either pass all 12 annual appropriations bills or pass another stopgap measure to avert a shutdown, adding another major legislative hurdle to an already compressed lame-duck session.

The Senate, meanwhile, is expected to hold a procedural vote Monday on advancing a bipartisan permitting reform package that would speed up the build-out of the nation’s infrastructure, especially energy projects.

Republicans have been divided over how to move forward as a conference, with some arguing that there needs to be a complete revamp of the leadership team.

“There has to be accountability for results, and you know the team that led us to the disaster probably isn’t the team that should lead us from the disaster,” one GOP lawmaker, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, told The Hill.

Jordan, co-founder of the far-right House Freedom Caucus, has emerged as a favorite among some House Republicans.

“I think we’re going into a wartime situation where we are going to be the rebel alliance, and we’re going to need someone who knows how to fight, and Jim Jordan knows how to do that,” the anonymous lawmaker said.

House Freedom Caucus Chair Andy Harris (R-Md.) also threw his support behind Jordan, arguing Thursday on Newsmax that Jordan “is the type of communicator we need, communicating commonsense Republican conservative principles again, against the backdrop of what is going to be a DSA [Democratic Socialists of America] -dominated Senate and House Democrat majority.”

But other Republicans argue that Scalise is better positioned to take the top spot, given his current leadership role. Scalise initially won the Republican nomination to be Speaker in 2023, beating Jordan in a secret-ballot vote. But he withdrew from the race when it became clear he would not win enough support from his conference to get the votes needed on the House floor.

“Steve is the right guy for the job. Plain and simple. He’s a tried and tested leader, who has the experience to lead House Republicans for the next two years, and the chops to reclaim the majority in 2028,” a second GOP lawmaker, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said.

Republican Study Committee Chair August Pfluger (Texas) is challenging Emmer for the minority whip position, while GOP Reps. Greg Steube (Fla.) and Erin Houchin (Ind.) are going head-to-head against McClain for the Republican conference chair role.

Massie said on social platform X last week that he plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment against Hegseth unless the Defense secretary resigns. Most Democrats are expected to support the measure, but House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) has stopped short of endorsing it.

Massie had previously launched an effort to impeach Hegseth back in September, but House GOP leaders canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early, avoiding a vote on Massie’s resolution. But only temporarily.

The Kentucky Republican argued then that Hegseth violated “his oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States” and violated “his constitutional duty to take care that the laws be faithfully executed, especially with regard to the commission of war.” He added that Hegseth has “abused the powers of the Department of Defense.”

President Trump told ABC News’s Jonathan Karl last week that he has “every intention” of keeping Hegseth in the Cabinet, following reports that he was weighing whether the Defense chief should stay in the post after the midterm elections.

Hegseth also fired back at Massie last week, saying in a video clip posted to X that “a disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly.”

“Just like they tried against President Trump twice. You see, their policies don’t work, so their obsession with political theater disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents. It’s all about the politics of personal destruction,” Hegseth said. “Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that.”

He’s probably right on that score. Even if the House does impeach Hegseth, the Senate is not likely to remove him from power.

Lawmakers have just two weeks to make progress on government funding before leaving again for Thanksgiving recess — an effort that will be challenged by a crowded legislative agenda that includes the annual National Defense Authorization Act, a farm bill and other priorities.

The House has passed three of the 12 appropriations bills, while Senate appropriators have remained deadlocked over top-line spending levels. The bills the House has passed so far — funding military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs, the State Department, and agriculture and rural development — represent some of the lowest-hanging fruit.

Johnson is sure to face much tougher resistance — both from Democrats and within his party — when the topic shifts to funding other agencies, including the departments of Homeland Security, Defense, and Health and Human Services.

Democratic lawmakers told The Hill before the midterms that they are keen on getting the rest of the appropriations bills done. But with a short calendar and a contentious subject, the odds are stacked against them. Most observers think a short-term spending patch, known as a continuing resolution, or CR, is the most likely scenario.

Rep. Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee, told The Hill in a statement she doesn’t think anyone wants a shutdown, and one is not likely.

“Both Democrats and Republicans have expressed a desire to finish full-year funding bills before the end of this calendar year, and I am ready to do just that,” DeLauro said. “The American people want us to address the cost of living crisis and rein in this corrupt administration. With Democrats widely expected to be in the majority, we want to hit the ground running in the new year — not be forced to finish the work this Congress failed to complete.”

Rep. Andrew Clyde (R-Ga.), a member of the House Appropriations Committee, said in a statement before the midterms that “whether or not there is a government shutdown is entirely up to Senate Democrats, who inflicted the longest government shutdown in U.S. history on the American people last year.”

“My priority remains passing the most conservative and fiscally responsible appropriations bills possible, and I look forward to completing that work when we return to Washington in the coming weeks,” he added.

The upper chamber is expected to hold a procedural vote Monday on a permitting reform bill, dubbed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act.

The legislation would make changes to the nation’s environmental laws that could make it easier to build projects and make it harder to block them, with either lawsuits or other legal mechanisms.

It also has provisions that are expected to make it easier to build and approve power lines, in particular, which is key to getting more power onto the grid. Democrats have pushed for such reforms, saying they believe they will particularly bolster renewable energy.

Trump has gone after renewable energy projects, and the bill contains measures that would protect those that are already approved. This bill could prevent Trump or other Republicans from trying to cancel renewable projects.

The bill is expected to advance, but it could receive some pushback from progressive Senate Democrats who have called for the administration to restore climate funding it terminated for blue states.

“While such action may not fully address the wide range of concerns individual Senators have about various portions of this complex legislation, it would represent an important first step and carry far more weight with us and, more importantly, our constituents whose awards were illegally terminated, than mere informal assurances that the Trump administration will stop interfering with clean energy projects,” the liberal senators wrote in a letter to Democratic and Republican negotiators of the bill.

Rachel Frazin contributed to this report.

https://www.france24.com/en/americas/202.title: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina amid divisions over Milei’s austerity
https://www.france24.com/en/americas/202.author: FRANCE 24
https://www.france24.com/en/americas/202.text:
Pope Leo XIV was greeted on Sunday in Argentina with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei.

The pope arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay where he began his first trip of Latin America, the world's most Catholic continent where secularism is growing fast.

The visit is the first by a pontiff to the home country of the late pope Francis in nearly four decades.

Argentines are hoping that his arrival will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of the libertarian Milei.

Milei, who famously insulted Francis for his pro-poor teachings, greeted the head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics at the foot of his plane on arrival.

"Just like the World Cup unites us, hopefully the pope will too," said Liliana Deblauwe, a 68-year-old retired teacher who waited with hundreds of people in a square for a glimpse of the passing pontiff.

"I'd like him to bring peace, unity, and-it's not nice to say this but for him to kick out Milei because he's a bad person," said Maria Veronica Panza, a 52-year-old housewife waiting nearby.

READ MORE
Pope Leo in Latin America: Papal Politics and Peru

Leo is expected to speak out in defense of the vulnerable over the course of his four-day visit.

Several hundred people chanting "Papa Leon" and waving yellow-and-white Vatican flags gathered outside the presidential palace where he was hosted by Milei.

They were kept at a distance, behind anti-riot police barriers.

Brian Inacio Rodriguez, a 26-year-old job seeker, spent five days travelling overland from Ushuaia, at the very tip of South America, to see the pope.

"It was worth it to be near the holy father," he said, adding he hoped he brought "much peace to Argentina."

Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, he is on an ambitious 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.

In secular Uruguay, he condemned drug violence and urged an end to child poverty.

The Argentine stage of his visit aims to boost the flagging faith of a country left disappointed by Francis's failure to visit during his papacy.

It will also act as a litmus test of support for the Church.

Some 57.7 percent of people identified as Catholic in a recent University of Buenos Aires poll, down from around 90 percent in the 1960s.

Leo is expected to urge greater protection of society's most vulnerable in the wake of Milei's cuts, which have left millions on the breadline.

He will visit a home for disabled people and a prison and celebrate three open-air masses.

The Church has said it expects a total of seven million faithful at the various events.

READ MORE
Pope Leo urges men to respect wives amid Latin American femicide crisis

Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina's ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state, targeting public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.

The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power -- increasing to 32.3 percent in September.

A close ally of US President Donald Trump, with a similar attacking style, Milei had a tense relationship with Francis.

On the campaign trail the cost-cutting economist called his countryman an "imbecile" for championing social justice.

Once in office, however, he softened his tone but he continues to heap insults on the press and opposition.

His relationship with Leo has so far been cordial, but the local Catholic Church has heavily criticised him for treating key social services solely as a budgetary constraint.

Milei has also been criticized for restricting several democratic freedoms, including the right to protest.

But he maintains a loyal supporter base for drastically reducing inflation.

The pope is expected to urge greater protection of society's most vulnerable in the wake of cuts. The pontiff is expected in Argentina to speak out in defense of the vulnerable over the course of his four-day visit.

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Missing Person

Police say William went missing near the historic gold mining town of Walhalla in Victoria's east.  (Supplied: Victoria Police)

A 17-year-old boy from the Latrobe Valley is missing four days after getting lost while camping in Victoria's east.

William had taken his shirt off due to warm weather on Friday afternoon.

The search for the teenager has resumed this morning.

A 17-year-old boy missing in Victoria's alpine region has likely spent the weekend in just shorts and boots as snow fell on nearby mountains overnight.

William, whose surname has not been released by authorities, was camping with another teenager in Walhalla East, near Cowwarr, when he walked a short distance to another part of their camp near Stoney Creek Road and T2 Track, but failed to return.

Victoria Police Superintendent Melanie Hamshere said the teenager had taken his shirt off in warm weather on Friday afternoon because he expected a 20-minute walk.

"They'd gotten quite warm so he took his T-shirt off, as boys do, and he walked back up towards the location where he'd been dropped off to pick up some more stuff to bring down," she said.

William went missing near Walhalla on Friday, November 6. (Supplied: Victoria Police)

William had gone back to collect an esky, two pillows, a fishing tackle box and a brown tabletop and did not take his phone with him.

The esky was found a short way up the track.

A cold snap brought a late dusting of snow to some of Victoria's mountain ranges over the weekend.

At Mount Baw Baw, about 45 minutes' drive north-east of Walhalla, overnight temperatures dropped to below zero degrees Celsius on Saturday and Sunday.

On Sunday, William's mother Elizabeth Barclay told the ABC he was an inexperienced camper with a poor sense of direction in an unfamiliar area.

Police have resumed the search for the teen today and have set up a staging area at Cowwarr Recreational Reserve.

Authorities are hoping to speak with a bearded man and a woman who helped William's friend on Friday night. They were in an older white ute with a black canopy.

The teenager flagged the car down when he began looking for William.

"We're appealing to the public to try and identify that couple," Superintendent Hamshere said.

About 70 people searched for William on Sunday, supported by a police helicopter, water police and the dog squad.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/r.title: Families face 150km daily drive as more regional childcare centres close
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/r.author: Andrew Chounding
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/r.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Julienne Slade says dozens of families will be impacted by the closures.  (ABC News: Andrew Chounding)

Three towns in south-west Western Australia will lose their childcare centres from December.

Parents say they will have to take time off work or drive hundreds of kilometres a day to access other services.

The Australian Childcare Alliance says the closures follow a national trend, with hundreds of centres facing financial strain.

After working as a police officer across Western Australia for more than a decade, Julienne Slade made the switch to teaching to spend more time with her family.

The veteran officer worked in rural towns in the state's Great Southern and Pilbara regions before moving back to her hometown of Mount Barker, 370 kilometres south of Perth, to settle down with her husband and begin a teaching career.

However, news that one of the town's two childcare centre will close in December has cast a cloud over her plans.

"I couldn't believe it because that's the daycare centre I went to when I was a child. It's been operating for at least that long, if not longer," she said.

Julienne Slade says families have received little notice of the centre's closure.  (ABC News: Andrew Chounding)

The family is not alone, with childcare provider Uplyft announcing it will close centres in the neighbouring towns of Mt Barker, Kojonup and Katanning in the next six months.

Affected parents say they will have to drive hundreds of kilometres each day to access alternative services, or join waitlists for closer centres.

Ms Slade's husband works in agriculture and they both said the closure would impact their careers.

"We'll have to adapt work. I'll either need to take leave or my husband will have to not work," Ms Slade said.

"If he's home looking after the kids, that's lost income, sometimes up to $5,000 or $6,000 a day because of how sporadic his work is."

Uplyft will close two centres next month and a third in June. (ABC News: Andrew Chounding)

Uplyft announced closures to some of its centres across WA in October.

The company's chief executive, Jo Sadler, said Mount Barker and Katanning's closure were due to lease conditions and also resulted in the Kojonup branch being unviable.

"As a result of these two events, it will be unfeasible to continue with an isolated service operating out of Kojonup," she said.

"At this stage, the Mt Barker and Katanning centres will close by the end of December 2026, while Kojonup will close in the first half of 2027."

The ABC spoke to several impacted families who said they were scrambling to secure places at alternative centres, but faced waitlists and limited availability.

Ryan Colman says he will have to drive more than 150km a day to access another childcare service.   (ABC News: Andrew Chounding )

Kojonup mechanic Ryan Colman sends his two-year-old child to Uplyft five days a week, and said he does not know what he will do when the town's only centre closes.

"We don't have another option, unless we're driving 80 kilometres return twice a day … That's the only real option, but that throws another financial burden into the mix because it's more fuel," he said.

"We've got mortgages and bills and that's not helping with interest rates always going up."

Data from the Early Learning and Care Council of Australia shows 152 services permanently closed between 2024 and mid-2026, with a further 276 services at risk of closure by July 2027.

Nesha Hutchinson says hundreds of centres across Australia are under financial strain.  (Supplied: Nesha Hutchinson)

Australian Childcare Alliance vice-president Nesha Hutchinson said rising inflation and high running costs were driving the closures.

"It's absolutely a problem — not just in Western Australia but across the country — that regional, rural, remote services are being pushed to the brink of financial viability," she said.

"Month by month … we're hearing of hundreds of services closing across the country … It's not going to get any better in the short term."

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Fermin Lopez scored twice as Barcelona overcame an early deficit at Atletico Madrid to win 2-1 and go three points clear at the top of La Liga.

Barca’s win takes them three points clear of second-placed Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico, in third, after 12 games.

Giuliano Simeone opened the scoring in the 10th minute for the home side, turning home a close range volley from Julian Alvarez’s cross from the left.

The home side had a series of early chances as they sought to register an eighth straight win, but Fermin swept in an equaliser on the cusp of halftime after a ball broke to him in the box.

Lamine Yamal set up Fermin’s second goal in the 66th minute with an incisive pass, and Lopez fired past Jan Oblak with a first-time finish to silence the Metropolitano and secure a fifth straight away league win over Atleti for the first time.

“It was a very difficult match. The first half was tough, but we managed to come from behind and secure the win,” Barcelona midfielder Lopez told La Liga TV after the match.

“I think we were not being clinical enough. After the goal, we gained more confidence.

“Lamine [Yamal] has been very good. His pass for the second goal was half the goal itself. I’m very happy,” Lopez said.

“We wanted to go into the break as league leaders and get three points. The equaliser lifted a weight off our shoulders, and we had more control.

“We knew at halftime that we had to continue playing the way we finished the first half. I think the team produced an incredible second half, both defensively and offensively. We’re very happy.”

https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.title: Study informs statin discontinuation in older adults without CVD
https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.author: Katie Kalvaitis
https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/2.text:
Purpose-built for physicians

CHICAGO — Stopping statin therapy in older adults with multiple chronic conditions but no established cardiovascular disease may be a reasonable option, according to results from the STREAM trial.

Among nearly 1,900 adults aged 70 years and older who were randomly assigned to stop or continue their statin, discontinuation was noninferior to continued use for time to major CV events or death at 2 years, Nicolas Rodondi, MD, director of the Institute of Primary Health Care at University of Bern, Switzerland, said during a late-breaking science presentation at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions. The results were simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

When the researchers extended follow-up to 4 years, there was increased risk for CV events among a small number of older adults in the discontinuation group, Rodondi said.

The researchers reported no difference in quality of life, pain, falls, sarcopenia risk or medication adherence between the discontinuation and continuation groups.

“This is an important piece of an evolving puzzle about statins for primary prevention ... in older adults,” Karen Alexander, MD, professor of medicine at Duke University, said during a discussion of the trial at a press conference. “Deprescribing is something our patients are very interested in. We often get asked: ‘Which drugs can I stop?’”

The open-label, randomized controlled STREAM trial enrolled older adults (mean age, 77.5 years; 46.9% women) with at least two chronic conditions who were taking a statin for primary prevention of CVD. One-third had diabetes, 90% hypertension, 10% were current smokers, one-third had a family history of CVD and about 29% had cancer. Half of the participants were recruited by general practitioners.

The primary outcome was first occurrence of nonfatal MI, nonfatal ischemic stroke or death from any cause.

At 2 years, mean event-free survival time was 96.5 weeks in the group randomly assigned to statin discontinuation and 98.5 weeks for the group assigned to continuation, for a difference of 2 weeks between the groups (95% CI, –3.7 to –0.3; P < .001 for noninferiority), the researchers reported.

“For every 40 individuals who discontinued statins, there was one additional CV event over 2 years,” Rodondi said.

At a maximum follow-up of 4 years (median, 103 weeks), participants in the discontinuation group had higher rates of MI (1.6% vs. 0.6%), ischemic stroke (2.2% vs. 0.8%) and all-cause death (9.8% vs. 8%).

Serious adverse events were similar between the two groups.

Based on the results of STREAM, statin discontinuation in this population appears “generally safe,” but the decision to do so must be patient-centered, Rodondi said.

“If you have a very sick, old patient with a lot of other severe chronic conditions [and] likely not a long life expectancy, the 2-week difference [in event-free survival] might not be worth continuing to take a statin if they have other issues. ... For an older adult [who is] very healthy, with some other chronic conditions ... it may be wise to discuss [a plan] to continue a statin.”

“Although international guidelines generally support statin therapy in older adults with chronic conditions, some international guidelines recommend considering statin discontinuation in these persons or in selected circumstances, such as limited life expectancy,” the researchers wrote in NEJM. “Recent surveys also found that both older adults and general practitioners ranked lipid-modifying agents among the top candidates for deprescribing; our findings provide information for shared decision-making about cautious statin discontinuation when statins are used for primary prevention only. Although deprescribing inappropriate drugs in older adults appears to be safe, the results of our trial suggest that additional randomized trials of discontinuation are needed for specific drugs; the use of other cardiovascular preventive medications over the period of follow-up should also be assessed, because these cointerventions can bias results.”

Discussing the findings, Alexander said “what STREAM should not be interpreted as is that we should go and stop medicines for primary prevention. This was a noninferiority trial, and the noninferiority margin was set at 5.2 fewer weeks free of cardiovascular events at 2 years. And they did not [exceed] that noninferiority margin, which was great.

“That could be interpreted from that definition as safe. However, there were 2 to 2.4 fewer weeks free from the cardiovascular composite events with statin discontinuation. So, it was not as though there were no cardiovascular events accumulating, and you saw the rate at 4 years was higher in those who discontinued statins for cardiovascular events.”

Press conference moderator Amit Khera, MD, MSc, clinical chief of cardiology and director of preventive cardiology and epidemiology at the Peter O’Donnell Jr. School of Public Health at UT Southwestern Medical Center, said “the investigators used the word ‘safe’” to describe the results. “I might say ‘acceptable risk’ ... there was at least acceptable risk in deprescribing in the right population.”

Another key point, Alexander said, is that statin discontinuation did not make participants in this study feel better.

In STREAM, “these were people who were tolerating statins; they were selected to be randomized to stop. And those who stopped them didn’t feel any better. ... There are lots of reasons why people who are older don’t feel good, but it would seem as though stopping statins is not going to be the answer. ... Where I would head next, is I would say, ‘let’s talk about your likely benefit from statins, because we know that if you’ve got a lot of benefits, stopping them could contribute to more events in the next 2 years,” Alexander said.

Alexander said the decision to discontinue statins in this population requires shared decision-making.

“To do shared decision-making, we have to have evidence, and they provided us ... some really important evidence in the STREAM trial about what to expect when one deprescribes,” Khera said.

Rodondi N, et al. LBS.03. Late-breaking science: Hot topics in CVD prevention. Presented at: American Heart Association Scientific Sessions; Nov. 6-9, 2026; Chicago.

https://www.france24.com/en/technology/2.title: Nvidia to probe reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
https://www.france24.com/en/technology/2.author: FRANCE 24
https://www.france24.com/en/technology/2.text:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company’s board of directors said Sunday.

The announcement came after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom US intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.

Huang apologized in a message to the company, according to the Times. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia’s board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.

Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.

Nvidia has become a central player in the global race to develop artificial intelligence, with its chips powering many of the data centers and computing systems used to train and run AI models. Its advanced processors have also been a focus of US export restrictions aimed at limiting China’s access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.

The Times reported last month that US intelligence agencies had discovered that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times.

READ MORE
Nvidia's Huang announces new investments in French tech sector

Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.

President Donald Trump addressed the reports at his Halloween party, calling the situation “very complex” and saying he hoped everything was OK with Jensen Huang, who serves on the president’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. The president has called Huang “smart” and “amazing,” insisting that Huang accompany him on foreign trips.

“I've always found Jensen Huang to be very aboveboard,” Trump told reporters on Oct. 31, adding that the administration would look into the matter “very closely.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday as he was departing the US for a G7 meeting in Paris that he could not address the situation with Huang.

“I just can't comment because of the nature of it,” he told reporters. “And I also can't comment on an internal corporate matter that's going on with Nvidia.”

Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has regularly surpassed Wall Street’s earnings expectations in the past three years since its high-end chips emerged as AI’s best building blocks. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion in August.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/p.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Topic:
Missing Person

Search efforts are continuing for the missing man. (ABC Gold Coast: Heloise Vyas)

A major air and sea search is underway for a boatie missing on the Gold Coast.

Emergency services were called to the Boykambil Esplanade Boat Ramp at Hope Island about 5pm yesterday after reports the man was heard yelling for help.

Gold Coast water police are searching for the missing man. (ABC Gold Coast: Heloise Vyas)

Police say the 55-year-old man, who lives on a sailboat in the Broadwater, went missing when he tried to paddle his broken-down tinnie he had been working on onshore back to his sailing boat.

"Somehow he became separated from his boat and he's obviously ended up in the water," Acting Inspector Peter Venz said.

"The circumstances around that we don't know."

The tinnie was found at nearby Coombabah Creek last night.

Acting Inspector Peter Venz spoke to media earlier today. (ABC Gold Coast: Mark Rigby)

Acting Inspector Venz said the man was reported to be a strong swimmer with no known medical conditions, but he had badly cut his foot on barnacles earlier in the day.

"We've got our fingers crossed he's safely been able to swim to shore," he said.

Police scoured the area into the early hours of this morning and resumed their search at first light today.

Marine Rescue Queensland crews, water police, the Polair aircraft and a rescue helicopter have joined the search, as well as the police dive team.

https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.author: James Elton
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/n.text:
BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

Two retail workers have been charged over the alleged assault of a man accused of shoplifting at their store. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

A 33-year-old man was allegedly punched, stomped and strangled by two young shop employees in Katherine before "losing consciousness", after allegedly stealing items from the store.

In a statement, NT Police said the incident happened at 10:35am on Saturday at a store at a Katherine shopping centre.

Police said the 33-year-old allegedly stole items from the counter area inside the shop before fleeing, with the two retail workers chasing after him.

When the 18- and 20-year-old workers caught up with the man a short distance away, police allege they began a "prolonged physical assault", including "punching, kicking and stomping on him".

"It is alleged he was also strangled," NT Police said.

"He lost consciousness as a result of the assault, with nearby bystanders intervening to prevent further from occurring."

The 33-year-old man was taken to hospital and was subsequently discharged.

Police said the two store workers were also taken to hospital, having "injured their hands" in the alleged assault.

All three men were remanded in custody and will face Katherine Local Court today.

The 33-year-old is facing robbery charges, while the two young men will face charges related to the alleged assault, including an acts intended to cause serious harm offence and strangulation.

Police are urging any witnesses to the incident to contact them.

https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-.title: Hong Kong records nearly 18% rise in ransomware cases amid drop in tech crime
https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-.author: Jess Ma
https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-.text:
Fighting fire with fire, police deploy AI-powered detection system, including in Interpol operation, amid rise in attacks aided by such technology

“We understand that the use of AI obviously increases the speed of attacks, the volume and intrusiveness. The attacks will be more effective,” Lam warned.

In response to the growing threat, police have also developed an AI-powered system to speed up the detection of suspected fraudulent websites. It was used in a year-long joint operation with Interpol from last July to this June to remove more than 51,000 phishing links.

From January to September, Hong Kong recorded 21,573 cases of technology crime, an 11.5 per cent drop from 24,370 reported over the same period last year. Losses also dropped from HK$4.59 billion to HK$3.9 billion, marking a 15.1 per cent decrease.

Two categories of cybercrime which target companies – ransomware and hacking cases – showed different trends.

Ransomware cases rose by 17.6 per cent to 40 in the first three quarters of this year, compared with 34 over the same period last year. Hacking cases dropped 21.6 per cent from 37 to 29.

Lam attributed the rise in ransomware cases to hackers’ use of various kinds of the technology, including AI, to probe corporate computer systems for vulnerabilities. He added that AI had also greatly reduced the costs of attacks.

“They use generative AI, agentic AI and automated AI to power the attack chain, so everything is just automated,” Lam said.

The chief superintendent urged companies to secure their computer systems by ensuring they were up to date, to prevent operational disruptions from cyberattacks.

“This situation reminds us that even though overall technology crime cases seem to have dropped, it doesn’t mean every single online threat has reduced correspondingly,” he warned.

In addition to local exercises to detect and neutralise cyberthreats, the force also deployed its own AI analysis engine, named Rapid, for the year-long operation with Interpol.

The engine analysed source codes, websites and web domain indicators to identify suspected fraudulent online entities.

The operation investigated more than 57,000 phishing links, removed over 51,000 of them and shared intelligence with 47 jurisdictions across over 10 Asian countries and at least two European states. Around 1,700 victims were identified.

Enrique Hernandez-Gonzalez, assistant director of cybercrime operations at Interpol, said the operation marked the first time the organisation had used an AI-powered system to identify and crack down on cybercrime.

“Our ultimate aim remains the rapid disruption of malicious infrastructure,” Hernandez-Gonzalez said.

The force also detected around 1.3 million instances of online hazards targeting the city in the first three quarters of this year, a 32 per cent jump from 1 million over the same period last year.

Among these detected threats, 350,599 were online phishing hazards, which accounted for the largest proportion at 27.6 per cent. This was followed by 321,393 instances of system scanning threats, at 25.3 per cent, and 210,211 instances of malware, at 16.5 per cent.

Lam attributed the rise in threats targeting the city to a global increase in cyberthreats, as well as heightened detection by the force.

Superintendent Rachel Hui Yee-wai, also of the cybersecurity and technology crime bureau, said the force reported more than 44,000 high-risk cybersecurity loopholes to relevant organisations for immediate fixes.

Among them were 37,950 loopholes concerning remote desktop protocol, which allows users to operate a computer system remotely, while another 6,083 concerned the PHP programming language, used in various e-commerce and enterprise portals.

The Digital Policy Office ordered all government bureaus, departments and public bodies to review their systems to see if they had been affected by a global discovery of vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language last month.

“Online infrastructure with unfixed loopholes tends to become a gateway for hackers to attack. Once a device is attacked, it could become a botnet,” Hui warned.

A botnet is a network of private computers, servers or devices infected with malware and controlled remotely by a single attacking party.
