https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: Gaza authorities slam global ‘inaction’ after mudslide kills five people
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
Palestinian authorities have criticised global “indifference and inaction” after a landslide killed five displaced people sheltering in tents in the central Gaza Strip following heavy rains.

“This is a scene that should shame the conscience of humanity and reflects the extent of the complicity and abandonment to which our […] people are subjected,” the Gaza Government Media Office said in a statement on Monday.

Four children and a woman were killed and two people remain missing after a sandbank collapsed onto their tent in Deir el-Balah on Sunday. The landslide happened after heavy rains brought by the first winter storm of the year hit the besieged territory on Friday, causing widespread flooding.

Floodwaters have inundated displacement camps and weakened buildings already damaged by Israeli air raids.

Restrictions imposed by the Israeli military mean specialist search and rescue equipment is in short supply, and Gaza residents were forced to dig using their bare hands to try and reach survivors.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah, Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum said the victims were living in flimsy tents, on exposed ground, with no protection from the heavy rain.

“When the embankment collapsed, those people had no chance to escape or protect themselves, and this raises difficult conditions about what people on the ground are left to endure,” he said.

About 70,000 tents were flooded when the storm hit Gaza at the weekend. According to data from Save the Children, more than half a million children are living in “critical or catastrophic” shelter conditions.

In a statement, Save the Children said, “While the so-called ceasefire announced over a year ago stipulated the entry of caravans as a more durable alternative to tents, Israeli authorities have repeatedly blocked their entry into Gaza, leaving hundreds of thousands of children exposed to another winter of hardship.”

The Government Media Office held Israel, the United States and the international community “fully and directly responsible”, citing their “absolute silence regarding the occupation’s crimes and their complicity in preventing the entry of shelter supplies, construction materials, caravans, fuel, and spare parts required to operate municipal and Civil Defence machinery and equipment”.

“We strongly condemn and denounce the state of inaction and the complete absence of the Board of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, as though this catastrophe were of no concern to them. Their complete failure to act and their flagrant abdication of the responsibilities entrusted to them raise serious questions about the very purpose of these bodies, which remain passive observers in the face of the suffering of the Palestinian people.”

More than 74,600 people have been killed since Israel’s genocidal war began on October 7, 2023, in response to a Hamas-led attack on southern Israel. Since a “ceasefire” took effect in October 2025, Israel has killed more than 1,600 Palestinians.

The landslide happened after heavy rains brought by the first winter storm of the year hit the besieged territory on Friday. More than 70,000 tents were flooded when the storm hit Gaza at the weekend.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China spy scandal?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.author: Usaid Siddiqui
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing questions over allegations that a Chinese businesswoman with whom he had a romantic relationship was gathering intelligence for Beijing.

Huang – who cofounded Nvidia, the world’s second-most valuable company after Apple, more than three decades ago – admitted on Sunday to being unfaithful to his wife, but the company said it has no reason to believe United States national security or confidential information has been compromised.

Nevertheless, Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation into whether the 63-year-old Taiwan-US dual national had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation after media reports linking him to Alice Huang, a former executive at a Singapore-based data centre company.

“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” it said in a statement, adding that Jensen Huang fully backs the review.

After the revelations, Nvidia – whose market capitalisation of $4.5 trillion is higher than the gross domestic product (GDP) of Japan, the world’s fourth-largest economy – saw its stock price tumble by more than 4 percent in trading overnight into Monday.

The controversy erupted as Washington seeks to prevent China from obtaining advanced American semiconductors, including Nvidia’s most powerful artificial intelligence chips, as the US and China fiercely compete for AI supremacy.

So what do we know about the affair, and how will this impact US-China relations and the race for AI dominance?

The allegations first emerged in a New York Times investigation late last month, which reported that US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang had been recruited by Beijing to gather information about Nvidia’s chief executive and potentially influence the company’s chip sales to China.

However, the precise nature of the information she allegedly obtained, whether any sensitive material was passed to Beijing and how much Jensen Huang knew about the alleged operation remain unclear. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are not related despite sharing a last name.

The two were reportedly seen together at industry events, including a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang in Taipei during the Computex technology exhibition in 2025.

On Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged his infidelity in a staff memo.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said.

However, in late October, Jensen Huang had told Bloomberg News that his interactions with Alice Huang were related to her company, Megaspeed, describing them as “completely normal and not unusual”.

Also known as Huang Le, Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen and former senior executive at Megaspeed International, which provides computing infrastructure used to operate and train AI systems.

According to The New York Times, Megaspeed had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing about $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.

A profile of Alice Huang found in a Chinese investment database listed previous employment at HSBC and Chinese television broadcasters CCTV and Hunan TV, according to the AFP news agency, which said it could not independently verify those details.

Alice Huang has not publicly responded to the espionage allegations, and her whereabouts are currently unknown.

Nvidia has launched an independent investigation overseen by a committee of directors and external legal counsel to determine whether its president and CEO was targeted by foreign intelligence.

The company said it had no reason to believe national security or its proprietary information had been compromised while expressing confidence in Jensen Huang’s leadership.

“The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate,” it said, adding that Jensen Huang has pledged to cooperate with the investigation and continue leading the company.

However, the allegations have unsettled investors.

“It deals a blow to the cult of Huang that has taken over the chip world in recent years,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at Britain’s IG Group, a leading derivatives trading firm, told Al Jazeera, while adding that it was too early to determine whether this moment might prove a “major turning point” for Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

“If this turns into a broader congressional investigation, then the shares are likely to come under pressure,” Beauchamp added. “As we learned from the financial crisis [in 2008 and 2009], once you go looking for skeletons in a cupboard, you usually find them.”

Jensen Huang’s daughter, Madison, who also works at Nvidia, cancelled a planned visit to South Korea for an Nvidia AI event amid the controversy.

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over suspicions that the company helped China obtain advanced Nvidia chips in violation of US export restrictions.

However, no criminal charges against Jensen Huang or Alice Huang have been reported. The controversy has prompted bipartisan pressure in Washington.

Republican lawmakers on Wednesday called on Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on November 18, arguing that the allegations raise serious questions about China’s potential access to sensitive US technology.

“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republican Congressmen John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren has also demanded answers from Nvidia and called for stronger legislation to prevent advanced US technology from reaching China.

“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China,” she said in a statement.

President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has defended Jensen Huang, describing him as an “honourable guy”.

Asked whether he should have acted after reportedly receiving an intelligence briefing about the allegations, Trump said, “No, I don’t think so.”

Meanwhile, ⁠⁠⁠⁠Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson ⁠⁠⁠⁠Guo Jiakun on Monday said the “so-called ⁠⁠⁠⁠Chinese spy ⁠⁠⁠⁠narrative” was unsubstantiated. “It is nothing but smears against China,” Guo added.

Jensen Huang, who is seen as a close adviser to Trump on the AI trade, has repeatedly pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China.

The scandal threatens to intensify tensions between Washington and Beijing over access to the powerful semiconductors needed to develop advanced AI systems. Semiconductors are needed to run nearly all electronics from smartphones to cars and military equipment.

Nvidia is a central player in that competition, supplying chips used by major US technology companies to train and operate AI models. It was until October 30 the most valuable company in the world.

“AI is now a technology that is really shaping national economies and GDPs, and safeguarding becomes even more serious. So protecting not only confidential secrets but also advancements for geopolitical reasons becomes even more important,” Fazl Barez, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford specialising in AI safety and governance, told Al Jazeera.

Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China over national security concerns. Nvidia’s top-of-the-line Blackwell GPU chips are banned for export to China.

The US has also clarified that restrictions apply to Chinese-owned companies operating outside China amid concerns that overseas subsidiaries could provide a route around export controls.

However, in December, Trump said Nvidia could sell its H200 chip to China, marking a major easing of US export restrictions. The H200, while not Nvidia’s top chip, is roughly six times more powerful than the model previously approved for sale to China, the H20.

The allegations surrounding Megaspeed could, therefore, increase pressure on Washington to scrutinise Nvidia’s overseas customers and tighten controls on chip shipments.

“Huang has been fairly explicit in his desire to let Nvidia sell to China. That now comes under threat,” Beauchamp said. “We are likely to see the US look to limit exports of the most complex chips, which of course will drive China harder to produce its own versions.”

So far, the US is putting far more private money into AI. In 2025, US private investment in the industry reached $285.9bn, compared with $12.4bn in China, according to Stanford University’s AI Index.

However, Chinese companies have continued developing competitive AI systems despite restrictions on advanced US chips.

In January, the release of the Chinese AI start-up DeepSeek‘s AI model made headlines after it was built using only a fraction of the money its competitors had spent on their own AI models. Share prices of US tech companies plummeted.

China has advantages in other areas of the AI supply chain, most notably in the production of critical rare earth minerals used in advanced technology. It also generates more than twice as much electricity as the US, giving it access to the vast amounts of relatively cheap power needed to operate AI data centres.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife on Sunday. The company said it has no reason to believe national security or confidential information has been compromised. The scandal threatens to intensify tensions between Washington and Beijing over access to the powerful semiconductors needed to develop advanced AI systems.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Usman Khawaja’s ‘Sandpapergate’ claims are ‘accurate’, says David Warner
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Former Australian cricketer David Warner has backed up claims made by former teammate Usman Khawaja, who said that their entire team had been aware ⁠⁠⁠⁠of the plan to ⁠⁠⁠⁠tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test tour of South Africa.

Warner spoke about the scandal, which continues to reverberate six years on, in a social media post on Monday, saying ‌‌‌‌that Khawaja’s comments were “100 percent accurate”.

The former Australian opener and fellow batters Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned over the plan ⁠⁠⁠⁠to rough up the ball with sandpaper during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town in 2018.

In a video posted on Instagram, Warner thanked Khawaja and said the investigation by Cricket Australia ‌‌‌‌into the incident was flawed.

“This whole interview process was rushed and botched,” added Warner, who retired from international cricket in 2024.

“Uzzie was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft. Uzzie was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me.”

In an excerpt from his autobiography released on Saturday, Khawaja said “open, lighthearted discussions” about tampering were not ⁠⁠⁠⁠confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.

On Sunday, he added that he had chosen to speak about the ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal now after promising childhood friend Warner that he would share his side of the story.

Cricket Australia has not commented on the statement issued by Warner, who said that he and Khawaja were looking for accountability.

“We’re not here to point fingers and we’re not opening old wounds,” added the 40-year-old.

“It’s about accountability, transparency ⁠⁠⁠⁠and ensuring the truth is properly examined and perhaps it’s time people ⁠⁠⁠⁠stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible of the investigation to provide it.”

“Now, there was a lot of statements and inaccuracies over the last eight years that were put out in the media by people ⁠⁠⁠⁠and there were a lot of people who stayed silent,” Warner said.

Last week, Cricket Australia defended its 2018 probe which concluded that prior knowledge of the ⁠⁠⁠⁠plot was confined to Smith, Warner and Bancroft.

“All relevant information ⁠⁠⁠⁠presented to [Cricket Australia] to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process,” it said in a statement on Saturday.

“There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the ‌‌‌‌case.”

The four Australian bowlers who played in the 2018 Test – Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon – issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot.

Cummins, now ‌‌‌‌the ‌‌‌‌Australian Test captain, said last month he had spoken with Khawaja about the upcoming release of his autobiography and dismissed suggestions that the book could trigger further fallout.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: At least four people killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
Overnight strikes between Russia and Ukraine have killed at least four people and damaged a Russian oil refinery.

A ⁠Russian ⁠attack on Ukraine’s port ⁠city of Odesa killed three people, the head of the ‌city’s military administration said on Monday. One other person was wounded and was in ⁠serious condition.

The ⁠⁠Kirishi refinery in Russia’s ⁠⁠Leningrad region was also set on fire in a Ukrainian ‌‌drone attack, Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Monday in a post on Telegram.

One woman was killed by falling drone debris, Drozdenko said.

The Ukrainian military’s chief of staff said Ukraine also hit the Morozov plant near St Petersburg, which produces explosives and fuel for Russian missiles used against Ukraine.

Also on Monday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that his country had agreed to establish a new mechanism to allow European Union funds to be deployed more quickly in response to Russian attacks  against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

The Kirishi refinery is Russia’s ⁠⁠second largest, and the Leningrad region is a major hub ‌‌for the country’s oil and grain exports via the Baltic Sea.

Leningrad’s governor also said air defence forces downed 113 Ukrainian drones and an apartment in Kirishi ⁠⁠had been damaged in the ⁠⁠same overnight attack on the region.

Russian forces also struck three ⁠⁠power substations and ‌‌a cargo ship in the Black Sea that Moscow ⁠⁠said was providing ⁠⁠arms to Ukrainian forces, Russian state ⁠⁠news agencies ⁠⁠reported.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify these claims.

Russia has attacked Ukraine’s energy sector 128 times ⁠over the ⁠past week, according to Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy. It said the attacks are part of a long-term campaign to degrade Ukraine’s energy and heating infrastructure before the winter.

“Right now, many of our cities and communities are facing a very difficult situation with power, water, and heating supplies due to Russian strikes,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X on Monday.

The president said he had agreed with Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, to “activate a special emergency mechanism” that would allow European funding “for what is needed most”.

“Our teams are already working on this,” Zelenskyy added.

The Kyiv, Dnipro, Sumy and Donetsk regions as well as Kherson are facing the most acute energy crises, the Ukrainian president said.

The Kremlin insisted on Monday that this week’s negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States will remain in the “trilateral” format. That followed French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot saying Europe would be represented at Tuesday’s talks and France would participate.

“What is set to take place in Abu Dhabi are trilateral negotiations between Russia and Ukraine under the mediation of the United States,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

“As for the Europeans, there are separate channels of communication between the Ukrainians and Europeans as well as the Americans and Europeans,” Peskov said.

Zelenskyy said he has coordinated negotiating positions in his talks with von der Leyen before the Abu Dhabi talks.

“We are doing everything to ensure that the trilateral format delivers results,” Zelenskyy said.

US President Donald Trump stoked fears that Washington would side with the Kremlin when he announced plans for a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only Ukraine but “all of Europe”.
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he has agreed to establish a new mechanism to allow European Union funds to be deployed more quickly in response to Russian attacks on Ukraine. Ukraine's government says Russia has attacked Ukraine’s energy sector 128 times over the past week.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: Iran’s authorities harden domestic security controls amid US strike threats
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
Iran’s domestic security apparatus is on high alert and hardening its approach in dealing with issues that authorities perceive to be jeopardising their control of the country during the war with the United States.

Iranian authorities have issued warnings to the public about tough sentences if they protest against the government and are tightening their control in public spaces after months of loosened restrictions on how people dress.

In short, the Iranian authorities appear to be trying to project an image that they will not yield on the principles of the Islamic Republic after eight months of war and amid the threat of a new, wider, more intense wave of US attacks.

Mahjoob Zweiri, director of the Gulf Studies Center at Qatar University, said the authorities have also been able to publicly mobilise supporters dedicated to the continuity of the government in Tehran amid these tensions.

“They include not only IRGC but also some civilians, and this is likely to continue until the war finishes,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), a military entity established to safeguard the principles of the 1979 Islamic revolution.

Iranian authorities routinely deploy harsh punishments to deter any form of dissent. The war, which began on October 28 with US and Israeli strikes on Iranian leaders, has only accelerated this process.

On Sunday, the judiciary said three young men arrested during nationwide protests in January were executed for allegedly attacking government offices and damaging public property near Tehran to benefit the US and Israel.

The authorities consider the antigovernment protests a “coup” attempt by “terrorists” affiliated with the US and Israel. But an independent United Nations fact-finding mission found the authorities had committed crimes against humanity during a violent crackdown on protesters that human rights groups said killed thousands of people, mostly on the nights of January 8 and 9.

Foreign-based rights organisations said many political cases that result in executions are marred by allegations of torture, forced confessions and other violations of due process.

This year, Iran’s government has executed at least 79 political or religious prisoners, including 40 people arrested during the January protests, according to the Norway-based Hengaw Organization for Human Rights. Some were executed after espionage convictions.

“Iran is a country at war with the world’s lone superpower, whose strategy toward Tehran remains unclear, and with Israel, whose government pursues a declared policy of overthrowing the regime in Tehran, whether through economic and military warfare or by partitioning Iran through a US- and Israeli-backed civil war,” political scientist Ali Alfoneh said.

“Taking these circumstances into consideration, the authorities of the Islamic Republic are no more repressive than any other regime facing similar threats.”

In some cases, authorities have loosened their enforcement of laws on the mandatory headscarf, the consumption of alcohol, the use of narcotics and other social issues in what Alfoneh said was in part to keep people busy with activities that might distract them from political activism.

“Repression appears to be reserved for matters of political freedom and for antiregime uprisings,” Alfoneh said.

There are signs that authorities are now cracking down on what they perceive to be public opposition to the principles of Iran’s theocracy as the war continues.

In Tehran on October 30, hundreds of mostly Gen Z Iranians celebrated Halloween by wearing makeup or costumes and gathering in cafes on artsy Iranshahr Street.

Within hours, motorcyclists and plainclothes security personnel arrived to disperse the crowds and close down cafes. Assaults and detentions were reported. People enjoying the evening in nearby Artists Park were reportedly ordered away.

The authorities did not officially comment on the incident but have since set up pro-government stations and booths on the same street, where supporters chant “revolutionary” slogans in praise of the government and wave flags.

Pro-government demonstrators have blocked city squares and streets in Tehran since the war began in perceived messages of defiance to domestic and external opponents.

As part of the “self-sacrifice” Janfada campaign, some of them receive gun training and other support at these locations to serve as part of the Basij, a domestic IRGC paramilitary force, which has been used to crack down on antigovernment protests.

Even before Halloween, police criticised gatherings on Iranshahr, Sanai and other streets in Tehran that have become popular gathering spots for young Iranians looking for space to express themselves amid deteriorating living conditions resulting from the war, an economic crisis and domestic mismanagement.

“Those streets have unfortunately turned into a place where people cruise and walk around,” Tehran traffic police chief Teymour Hosseini said last month. He also hinted that the gatherings of young people were the reason cafes and businesses have been shut down by police in recent months.

The government also continues to impose a dress code, especially for women, since shortly after the 1979 revolution. But since the nationwide Mahsa Amini protests of 2022-2023, women have increasingly ditched their headscarves in public in Tehran and other cities in defiance of the law.

Hossein Shariatmadari, a hardline media figure, wrote in an article that loose hijabs were “one of the levers used by the enemy in the coming war” and must be taken seriously.

“The enemy has been defeated in military confrontation with Islamic Iran and has now shifted a considerable part of its abilities towards war in economic and cultural areas, particularly through expanding loose hijab,” he said.

State crackdowns have also attracted some limited attention in local media although for different reasons.

“A tense night in Iranshahr”, the reformist Shargh newspaper wrote about the operation on the eve of Halloween, urging policymakers to study what people want and provide attractive cultural opportunities. The Rouydad24 news website questioned the usefulness of treating the cultural preferences of young people as security problems.

The ultraconservative Keyhan newspaper wrote that Halloween celebrations were evidence of “cultural alienation” that was weakening knowledge of ancient traditions like Nowruz, the Persian New Year.

But Iranian authorities over the years have politicised domestic traditions too, namely by restricting and shooting at Chaharshanbe Suri fire festival celebrations during the protests.

Qatar University’s Zweiri said whether Iran and the US manage to end the war through a negotiated resolution or engage in a more devastating conflict would play a role in determining if more nationwide protests take place in Iran.

Some Iranians feel that any kind of protest currently could be interpreted as allying with foreign powers.

“The second level of reality is the identity of being Iranian, which means no Iranian wants to be affiliated to an enemy that attacks and destroys the country,” Zweiri said.

“Whether there is a deal or more war in the future will determine how Iran will be developing economically and politically and socially.”

Authorities have politicised domestic traditions too, including restricting and shooting at fire festival celebrations. Some Iranians feel that any kind of protest currently could be interpreted as allying with foreign powers.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: Qatar PM to meet Trump: What’s the latest on US-Iran negotiations?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.author: Al Jazeera Staff
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
United States President Donald Trump is set to hold talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani behind closed doors at the White House on Monday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to bridge differences over Iran’s nuclear programme and the terms for ending the conflict.

An unnamed US official told the Reuters news agency that Vice President JD Vance is also scheduled to hold talks with Sheikh Mohammed, who also serves as foreign minister and has been known to act as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran.

Iran has stepped up diplomatic efforts amid suggestions by Trump that the US could resume full-scale strikes on Iran.

Here is a look at where diplomatic efforts stand before the meeting:

Iran offered the US a new nuclear and peace proposal via Qatari mediators on Thursday, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran’s seven demands. The US is examining the proposal.

Iran has been unwilling to hold negotiations over its atomic activities with the Trump administration until the latter agrees to several core conditions that Tehran has been demanding be part of any ceasefire agreement.

Tehran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9kg (972 pounds) of uranium that is enriched up to 60 percent purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90 percent.

Iran’s enrichment boost came after Trump withdrew from the nuclear deal in 2018. Signed under President Barack Obama, the deal had capped enrichment at below 3.67 percent.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday warned that Tehran will “rain down hell” if the US resumes attacks.

Speaking to Al Jazeera last month, Araghchi said Tehran’s two-day proposal was developed with Qatari mediators and based on the seven-day plan Iran announced at the UN General Assembly in September.

“On day one, the US implements a set of measures. On day two, the Strait of Hormuz will reopen, and navigation will be restored to what it used to be,” he said.

Tehran’s demands include lifting the sanctions Washington imposed on Iran after the collapse of a memorandum of understanding, signed in Islamabad, Pakistan, in June, reducing the US military presence in the region, reinstating the oil waivers granted in June as part of the MoU and releasing frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar.

Tehran also requested that the new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz, a global oil chokepoint, worked out by Iran and Oman be formally recognised and that all other routes be closed. Finally, it demanded ending the war on all fronts, including Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Araghchi held talks with 12 regional counterparts over 48 hours last week, calling for a regional security arrangement free from the involvement of extra-regional powers. Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned Trump on Saturday against renewed attacks, saying: “Start war and you will face a devastating response.”

Trump on Sunday warned that Washington had identified additional targets in Iran should military action resume, but said it was “highly unlikely” to ‌launch new strikes if negotiations yielded a strong agreement.

Sheikh Mohammed said mediation efforts continue and that the US has intentions and willingness to “take steps towards finding a solution”, after Trump confirmed on Friday that the White House was talking to Iranian representatives and that the team had “made a lot of progress with Iran”.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said negotiations with Iran had not made progress. He told reporters in Florida on Sunday that while the war was unpopular, Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and had worked to stop it from pursuing a nuclear weapon.

Rubio added that although the US president prefers a diplomatic solution, Iranian demands are “not just unacceptable, but in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”.

“I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough,” he added.

US media reported that Trump was being pressed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Brad Cooper to resume attacks against Iran.

Axios quoted a US official as saying CENTCOM was preparing for the resumption of major military operations in Iran, and that it was just waiting for orders from Washington.

On Thursday, Trump told reporters the US may have to “destroy” the rest of Iran, adding that people will “know soon enough” if he acts.

Trump warned that US forces have three aircraft carriers stationed in the region “fully locked and loaded”, ready to continue strikes if need be. He said the US identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that it would strike if military action resumes.

The US military, meanwhile, has carried out limited strikes on Iran, including against its air defences, at least twice over the past week. It also fired on a commercial ship and disabled it on Saturday, which the US said was trying to breach its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Rubio said Washington would take “defensive” actions if needed. “If there’s a clear and present threat to shipping or to our forces in the region, we have a right to defend ourselves,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Aerospace Force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday made threats that echoed those of the Iranian foreign minister and said weapons have been “secured for years to come”.

IRGC Brigadier-General Ali Belali said in a statement on Telegram that “the armed forces are at the ready, and if the enemy makes a mistake, Iran’s response will be devastating and severe.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.title: Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ for voters
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9.text:
United States President Donald Trump has said his immigration policy may have been too extreme for voters, conceding that his deportation policy had damaged his Republican Party’s performance in the last week’s midterm elections.

During his first television interview since his party lost control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate last week, Trump said some voters were unhappy with his administration’s controversial deportation drive, which led to widespread protests.

“I think it might be too tough,” he told CBS’s 60 Minutes programme, which aired on Sunday.

He said he may be able to work with the new Democratic-controlled Congress on some kind of immigration agreement.

“The deal would be we would work something out,” he said, adding, “I think that’s something that’s actually doable.”

The interview was aired after he appointed Stephen Miller, the chief architect of his hardline immigration policy, to replace Susie Wiles as his White House chief of staff, prompting questions about the direction of his immigration policy.

In a post on X, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said, “Trump says his immigration crackdown went too far”, adding, “Apparently, his solution was to put the man responsible for it in charge of the White House. That’s not a course correction. That’s a promotion.”

Trump had promised an immigration crackdown during his campaign to return to office, blaming undocumented migrant “killers” and “drug dealers” for soaring crime.

Extensive operations to detain and deport immigrants were launched in multiple US cities, causing arrests to soar.

Two US citizens – Renee Good and Alex Pretti – were killed by federal officers during protests against the operations.

Democrats have said oversight of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Department of Homeland Security is a priority for the new Congress.

During his interview, Trump said a moderate immigration deal would still deport criminals, but allow “good people” who had lived and worked in the country “paying taxes” to stay.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/meet-d.title: Meet Drops, the new music app bringing back the fun of sharing songs with friends
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/meet-d.author: Lauren Forristal
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/meet-d.text:
There’s a new music discovery app borrowing the endless vertical-scrolling format of TikTok. But instead of watching videos, users swipe through short clips of songs, hoping to stumble upon their next favorite artist.

Launched Monday by Harman, a Samsung subsidiary, Drops aims to make discovering new music feel social again.

Available on iOS and Android in the U.S., the app lets users scroll through 10-to-30-second snippets of songs, accompanied by lyrics, album artwork, artist photos, and captions. The idea is to give listeners just enough of a track to grab their attention, whether it’s a particularly good lyric, a catchy hook, or a beat that makes them want to hear more.

The company says Drops is meant to feel like a return to how people used to discover music in the first place. Before every platform’s algorithm recommendations, people often heard about new songs through friends, music blogs, or online communities. Drops is trying to recreate that experience.

“You send a friend a song and say, ‘You have to hear this.’ Then you end up texting, ‘Skip to 1:47, that’s the best part.’ The part that hits usually isn’t the first few seconds, and there wasn’t a good way to share just that moment,” Clare Hunter, general manager of Drops, told us.

Hunter explained that the idea for Drops began taking shape after Harman acquired music management software company Roon in 2023.

“I used to spend hours making mixtapes for my friends, picking the songs, the order, and decorating the cover. Drops is the version of that I always wanted,” Hunter added.

The app is easy to navigate, with tabs including “For You,” “New,” “Showcase,” and “Following,” along with relevant and trending hashtags.

Users can like, comment, repost, share, and save tracks to collections called Droplists. They can also send songs directly to other users, follow other profiles, and exchange direct messages.

To listen to the entire track, Drops offers integrations with major streaming services, including Apple Music, Qobuz, and TIDAL. Users can jump directly into the full version of the song through their connected streaming platform.

Notably, the company says it doesn’t use generative AI for audio or visuals. Songs appear as they were originally released, using official album artwork and licensed artist photography. At a time when AI-generated music and slop are becoming harder to avoid, this will likely appeal to many users.

Another part worth noting is that Drops pays rights holders and reports plays back to its partners. Those partners include Universal Music Group, Beggars Group, Empire, Symphonic Distribution, and UnitedMasters.

Plays also count toward streams on those services, meaning Drops isn’t trying to replace existing music subscriptions.

Drops is currently invite-only, with U.S. users able to join the waitlist.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/meet-d.summary: Drops lets users scroll through 10-to-30-second snippets of songs, accompanied by lyrics, album artwork, artist photos, and captions. The app is available on iOS and Android in the U.S. and is currently invite-only.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/automa.title: Automattic debuts a platform to deploy vibe coding apps amid a changing internet
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/automa.author: Ivan Mehta
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/automa.text:
WordPress has been a crucial technology and content management system for websites like TechCrunch. Now, WordPress.com owner Automattic is responding to the changing state of the web by debuting a new service called Spacefast, which will allow users to deploy vibe-coded websites and apps.

Spacefast is designed to provide infrastructure for the vibe-coded apps, including databases, authentication, file uploads, emails, and analytics, to make them functional websites, apps, or services. The product competes with the likes of Lovable and Emergent, which offer both interface and rails for vibe-coded apps, but in a more open way.

Users can connect Spacefast with other agents and chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, Grokbot, Muse, Pi, Cursor, Opencode, and Amp. Alternatively, they can connect a Git repository to Spacefast to get started.

The product is headed by Batuhan İçöz, who worked on working on it during one of the company’s hackathon sprints earlier in the year. At that time, he worked on the company’s cross-platform messaging app Beeper and said that he often got Vercel links from his non-technical friends while exploring vibe coding.

“I thought there had to be a better way for everyone to set up and deploy their projects. Automattic already has good infrastructure, but we have been traditionally associated with just WordPress. I thought, why do I have to use Cloudflare when we have a CDN (Content Delivery Network) just as good? So I started working on what was called Stattic and now Spacefast,” he told TechCrunch over a call.

İçöz eventually disseminated the solution to his friends and added more features to make the product more dynamic. Automattic soft-launched the product in September to get feedback before today’s launch.

The company has seen varied use cases of their product, with people and organizations using it for internal mockups, slideshows, and offer-related websites. However, that’s not the only competition Spacefast has. Productivity and design software like Figma, Canva, and Notion have launched products that sit at the intersection of vibe coding, mockups, and presentations.

İçöz thinks that, compared to something like Lovable, Spacefast has the advantage of giving users a choice of their agent and using the solution their way. The counter-argument might be that a certain kind of user wouldn’t want to choose and just have everything figured out for them.

Spacefast said that it also has the advantage of being within Automattic to launch solutions like web analytics, WordPress integration, and e-commerce features (through WooCommerce) easily to compete better with the whole lot.

“For enterprises, the problem right now is IT sprawl, as their marketing teams are churning out landing pages on services like Lovable, and they want to consolidate and work with a company that understands the enterprise needs. With our existing products, we have experience serving enterprise customers,” İçöz noted.

A challenge for newly minted products in the AI world is to retain people post-launch. Users might get excited to try out a new product, and then move on to the new shiny thing within days or weeks. İçöz is cognizant of the fact and said that he expects people to churn, as they might not be interested in making apps at all.

“I think what we need to do as a product is make sure that when you build something with SpaceFast, it is so easy, and the results are so much better than without Spacefast,” İçöz emphesized.

Many websites and publishers are struggling with dwindling traffic due to AI chatbots and summaries, right now, to the point that Google itself saw its ad revenue growth drop. İçöz acknowledged that people are making websites with ChatGPT or Claude now as compared to deploying something on WordPress, and he said some sites won’t need a content management system at all as the web expands.

Spacefast comes amid turbulent months at Automattic. In an OpenAI-Sam Altman-style saga, the company’s board forced CEO Matt Mullenweg out, but he was back in control within days. The rebel board was eventually replaced, and the interim CFO left within weeks of appointment. In October, TechCrunch reported that the company had began layoffs across several properties and more cuts were expected.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/automa.summary: Spacefast is designed to provide infrastructure for vibe-coded apps. It will allow users to deploy vibe- coded websites and apps. Spacefast is headed by Batuhan İçöz, who worked on it during one of the company’s hackathon sprints earlier in the year.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/musk-s.title: Musk says Tesla will refund some Cybertruck deposits, defends decision to end production
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/musk-s.author: Kirsten Korosec
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/musk-s.text:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk is defending the Cybertruck and the company’s decision to stop producing the polarizing steel-clad truck, claiming that the order rate far exceeds its production.

Tesla will shut down production of the Cybertruck in about eight months Musk said in an X post on Monday. He also said the company will try to make as many of the vehicles as possible before then, though Tesla will “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

Musk argued the Cybertruck was not unprofitable, and that Tesla was ending production because the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.”

In other words, Musk is arguing that Tesla can make more money by using the factory space and resources dedicated to the Cybertruck for building Cybercab robotaxis. Musk said last week that Tesla plans to use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercabs.

The first Cybertrucks were delivered to customers in late 2023, when it seemed like it could be a breakthrough hit for the company. Reservations for the vehicle had ballooned to 1 million, according to Musk, who also predicted that the company would sell around 250,000 of the trucks annually.

But those reservations never translated into actual sales. Tesla doesn’t break out sales of the Cybertrucks, but industry experts estimate a total of about 71,000 Cybertrucks have been sold since the first deliveries began in November 2023.

Many of those sales came from inside Musk’s ecosystem of other businesses. For instance, SpaceX (now known as SpaceXSI), which he also leads and is the largest shareholder of, purchased $131 million worth of Cybertrucks from Tesla in 2025, according to the company’s S-1 registration statement ahead of its IPO. Another Musk company, xAI, also bought $430 million worth of Tesla Megapacks for its data centers, before it merged with SpaceX.

But sales of the Cybertruck, which lagged for months, could see a final bump now that it’s going out of production. Still, even a scarcity boost is unlikely to push the truck’s demand to the lofty projections from several years ago.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/musk-s.summary: Tesla will shut down production of the Cybertruck in about eight months. Musk said the company will try to make as many of the vehicles as possible before then.

https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/tesla-.title: Tesla expands robotaxi service to San Antonio
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/tesla-.author: Kirsten Korosec
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/tesla-.text:
Tesla is expanding its robotaxi service to another Texas city as it seeks to compete with Waymo and position itself as more than just an automaker. The company said in a post on X that it will make its robotaxis available in San Antonio starting at 5 a.m. local time on Monday.

Tesla didn’t provide any additional details about the service, such as the hours of operation, whether the fleet will offer customers its gold, two-seater Cybercab as well as its modified Model Y vehicles, or if these vehicles will have human safety monitors on board. But if the company follows its playbook of previous launches, it will start with a limited number of vehicles and a confined service area, and expand slowly from there.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk for a decade promised his company would deliver autonomous vehicles, and it eventually launched a robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025. The launch, though limited and supported by human safety operators on board, was an important milestone for the company and a test of whether self-driving cars could be safely deployed using just cameras and end-to-end AI.

Since then, Tesla has slowly expanded. In January, the company removed safety monitors from its robotaxis in Austin, officially kicking off a true driverless service, and has spent the last 11 months expanding within the city, and to new cities in Florida and Texas. It now operates robotaxis in limited areas of Miami and Orlando as well as Dallas, Fort Worth, and Houston.

Its rival Waymo also operates a robotaxi service using a mix of driverless Jaguar I-Pace and Zeekr RT vehicles, branded Ojai, in Austin, Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio. The company, a subsidiary of Alphabet, recently restarted services in San Antonio after a five-month pause following incidents in which its vehicles got stuck after entering flooded roadways.

While Tesla has more than 400 autonomous vehicles registered in its Austin fleet, its fleets in other cities have numbered between a handful and a few dozen, according to Texas vehicle registration data and the Robotaxi Tracker website. For example, Tesla has just 24 vehicles in Fort Worth and five in Miami, according to the tracker.

Tesla also has a ride-hailing service, under a transportation charter permit, that it operates in the San Francisco Bay Area. While the vehicles are often described as robotaxis, they are operated by a human behind the wheel. Tesla currently doesn’t have the required permits to operate a driverless ride-hailing service in California.

In spite of this expansion push, the company released data this summer that showed its robotaxi network drove fewer miles with paying customers in the second quarter than it did in the first, TechCrunch reported in July.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/tesla-.summary: Tesla will make its robotaxis available in San Antonio starting at 5 a.m. local time on Monday. The company didn’t provide any additional details about the service, such as the hours of operation. Tesla CEO Elon Musk for a decade promised his company would deliver autonomous vehicles.

Thankfully, like in previous years, we’ll be working to highlight the best prices on phones, TVs, noise-canceling headphones, gaming gear, and other tech throughout the deal-packed week, whether you plan to shop in person or online.

You can always count on us to publish the best deals that you need to know about, no matter the season. However, if you want to be among the first people to discover price drops on the products you’re interested in, you’ll want to get a head start on your Black Friday game plan. Your checklist should include scouting out early sales at your favorite retailers, setting up the right price-tracking tool, and configuring your alerts to ensure you don’t miss rare discounts at Amazon and elsewhere. Lucky for you, we’ve compiled several tips and tricks below to help you get started.

The most effective way to find a truly great deal is to set up a price-tracking tool. We’ve included a few of our favorite examples below, many of which we use on a daily basis here at The Verge. Each can help you track deals at various retailers — including Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Target — but they each do so differently and come with their own set of advantages / disadvantages.

All of them are free to use, and once you’ve added the products you’re interested in keeping an eye on, you can rest easy knowing that you don’t need to take any action until it comes time to make a purchase. Just make sure you keep your email notifications on so you see the alerts as they come in.

CamelCamelCamel tracks the price of every product sold on Amazon and can send you alerts when an item falls to a customizable threshold. Once a product reaches the desired price you’ve set or lower, you’ll get an email about it. You can use the extension’s price graph to determine what price is likely to happen, but it’s always a shot in the dark. The tracker also only works for products listed on Amazon, so you’ll need to use one of the alternate trackers featured below if you want to track price fluctuations at Walmart, Best Buy, and other retail sites.

To track prices and get alerts via email, you’ll need to create a free CamelCamelCamel account. Additionally, we suggest installing the site’s browser extension, The Camelizer, which works with Google Chrome, Safari, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, and Microsoft Edge. The handy tool enables you to view pricing trends on a product-by-product basis and allows you to set your desired price without needing to navigate away from Amazon. It’s fantastic, easy to use, and works in several countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and Australia.

As soon as a product falls below the amount set on your price alert, you’ll instantly get an email. And if you already have a wishlist saved on Amazon, you can easily import it into CamelCamelCamel.

Like CamelCamelCamel, Keepa is another handy tool for tracking the prices of products on Amazon. Keepa has charts that track pricing trends and can alert you when it finds a deal. You can also import any of your Amazon wishlists.

Unlike CamelCamelCamel, however, you don’t necessarily need to create an account to track prices with Keepa; just install the appropriate browser extension, and Keepa will automatically add a price history graph to supported product listings. The embedded graph showcases pricing history and allows you to specify various pricing details. If you set a desired price, Keepa will send you a price alert via email, push notification, Telegram, or RSS.

Slickdeals aggregates some of the best deals around the internet, as discovered by its team and community of users. Its site also allows you to browse coupons and create deal alerts based on specific keywords, though the latter works a little differently on Slickdeals than it does with the above sites.

You can type in a product name, like “Nintendo Switch 2,” “OLED TVs,” or a retailer’s name, and once it’s added to your list, you’ll be notified of a deal alert if it meets your criteria. You can set it to alert you to literally any deal relating to your keyword, or you can filter out deals so that you’ll be notified if, for example, the deal is popular enough to make it to Slickdeals’ front page or if it earned a high rating from the community. If you like browsing deals, it’s generally good advice to visit Slickdeals frequently, especially since it usually has a Black Friday component that allows you to browse circulars for Best Buy, Target, and other retailers in advance.

For a more hands-off approach to seeing if you’re getting a good deal, try using your browser. For a few years now, Microsoft Edge has been able to tell you when you’re looking at the best price for a particular product from a range of retailers, and Google Chrome can track price fluctuations and notify you when a particular product goes on sale. Edge and Chrome are available on Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as Android and iOS.

If you have an Alexa-compatible smart gadget, such as the new Echo Dot Max or Echo Studio, you can ask the virtual assistant to alert you when specific products go on sale. You can receive alerts up to 24 hours in advance of planned price drops for eligible products, or as soon as it notices a discount on anything saved in your shopping cart or wish list. If you say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” after being notified of the deal, the assistant will purchase the item for you once the discount becomes available.

To enable these features, open the Alexa app on your smartphone and navigate to More > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping. Then, toggle the slider next to Deal Recommendations within the Shopping Recommendations section. Alexa will audibly notify you of deals moving forward, but if you happen to miss one, you can check for the notification on your phone or see whether you have any new notifications on an Echo device by checking for the yellow light. If it’s lit, just say, “Alexa, play notifications.”

You can receive similar notifications on your smartphone from the Amazon Shopping app, too. Just open the app and go to Settings > Notifications > Deals and recommendations, and toggle the slider next to the Savings option.

Keeping an eye on preferred retailers before Black Friday will help save you time (and money). Several major retailers have already detailed their plans in the run-up to the holidays, and many of them will be offering early opportunities to save. For example:

You can expect more major retailers, including Amazon, to detail their Black Friday plans shortly, so keep an eye on their respective websites and start filling your calendar accordingly.

Doorbusters, lightning deals, and other limited discount opportunities are a tried-and-true hallmark of any Black Friday sale. They’ll usually be the most buzzworthy deals you’ll see all year, with truly low prices to spark impulsive spending. As you’re checking ads, make special note of these deals and read all of the fine print surrounding their availability. Some may require you to sign up in advance or get in line early (ahem, Amazon), and some can be so scarce that you won’t have the entire weekend — or even an hour — to claim them.

Although many stores will automatically match their competitors’ pricing, sometimes, you may need to twist their arm. It’s helpful to know the various price-matching policies of each retailer in the event that your preferred store runs out of stock on certain goods. You can get up to speed with our price-matching guide, which details the lengths each retailer will or won’t go to win your dollar. Unfortunately, some retailers put a temporary halt on their usual policies during special shopping events like Black Friday, but it never hurts to ask.

We’re a discerning bunch here at The Verge, so don’t fret if you’re going into Black Friday / Cyber Monday without any prep. We’ll be corralling the best deals on tech and keeping our coverage up to date with new sale items while eliminating old ones to avoid any disappointment. While we usually suggest paying attention to deals starting the day after Thanksgiving — or November 28th, in this case — the truth is that several retailers typically jump the gun and start offering some great deals in the lead-up to the shopping holiday.

To catch every opportunity to save, be sure to bookmark our coverage, follow us on Bluesky, subscribe to our triweekly Verge Deals newsletter, and start putting a little spending cash aside for Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

https://www.theverge.com/21570383/price-.title: Here are the price-matching policies for Best Buy, Walmart, and others
https://www.theverge.com/21570383/price-.author: Sheena Vasani
https://www.theverge.com/21570383/price-.text:
With Black Friday approaching, we’re here to let you know which retailers will go the extra mile on your behalf.

With Black Friday approaching, we’re here to let you know which retailers will go the extra mile on your behalf.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Nothing is more frustrating than buying a new pair of headphones or an OLED TV, only to find out you could have gotten it cheaper somewhere else a few days or weeks later. That’s why, to keep customers happy and prevent them from shopping elsewhere, some retailers offer price-matching policies that promise to match a lower price found elsewhere. That kind of information comes in handy year-round, but it’s especially helpful during the weeks of deals leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Below are the price-matching policies for several major retailers. A few things to note: First, each retailer has its own set of rules and restrictions. We’ve summarized some of them here, but we recommend visiting the provided links and reading the policies carefully. Second, most retailers that serve as marketplaces for other sellers, including wholesale retailers like Costco, don’t offer protections, and many traditional stores won’t match their prices.

Lastly, there are always exceptions to the rules. If you’re looking for a deal on a product and you know it’s available for a lower price elsewhere (or it was previously offered at the same retailer), it never hurts to call or chat with a customer service rep and ask if they’ll match the price. You have nothing to lose but time, and there’s always a chance they may find a loophole or make a special exception.

Amazon doesn’t offer price matching. Full stop. You can contact customer support, but even if you’re an Amazon Prime customer, they likely won’t help. That said, the online retailer does offer a liberal return policy, meaning you can often return an item you purchased from Amazon if it’s available for less elsewhere (or at Amazon). Then, you can just repurchase the product wherever it’s cheapest.

Target used to let shoppers price match identical items sold by select retailers, including Amazon, but no longer does so. Under its current policy, shoppers can only request a price adjustment if they find an identical qualifying item for less than they paid on Target.com, at their local Target store, or through an eligible Target Circle deal. Target will also price match Target Plus Partner (the retailer’s name for third-party sellers) items if the same Target Plus Partner on Target.com has it for less, or with a Target Circle deal. Price matches can be requested at the time of purchase or within 14 days after purchase.

For the 2026 holiday season, Target has extended the aforementioned price-match window. If you purchase an eligible item between November 1st and December 24th, you can request a price adjustment if its price drops at Target during that period. The extended policy also applies to eligible Target Plus Partner purchases.

To request a price match, you’ll need to show the online price or digital version of the ad and provide your original receipt or packing slip; screenshots and photos aren’t accepted. Alternatively, you can call for online purchases at 1-800-591-3869 or chat online via contactus.target.com.

However, note that Target’s policy excludes in-store price matches from other Target stores. It also can’t be combined with Target Circle Bonuses, Target coupons, Registry coupons, or gift card promotions, and doesn’t apply to clearance, closeout, liquidation, damaged, used, open-box, refurbished, pre-owned, or rent-to-own items. In addition, Target won’t match prices between items sold directly by Target and those sold by third-party Target Plus Partner sellers.

Best Buy’s Price Match Guarantee states that a product could be eligible for a price reduction if it’s new, identical to the competitor’s product, immediately available at a qualifying competitor’s store or on its site, and not shown on Best Buy’s exclusion list — that includes “items for sale the Thursday before Thanksgiving Day through the Monday after Thanksgiving.” Items must have the identical model number and color. However, Best Buy only matches prices that are available to all customers and does not match membership-exclusive, loyalty-program, or paid-member discounts; thus, it excludes events like Amazon Prime Day.

To get the difference for online purchases, you have to contact Best Buy via its on-site chat and provide the ad or website with the lower price. Alternatively, you can call 1-888-237-8289 or visit any Best Buy or Pacific Sales store. Approved retailers include Amazon, B&H Photo, Apple, Costco, Sam’s Club, Target, and Walmart. Items must be sold directly through the store, too, not a third-party seller.

Best Buy will also, upon request, match an in-store or online price that was lowered during the return and exchange period, which typically lasts up to 15 days. Keep in mind that the return window on most products is 60 days for both Best Buy Plus and My Best Buy Total members. For the holiday season, however, most eligible products purchased between October 30th and December 31st can be price matched through January 15th, 2027, if Best Buy lowers its own price. This policy doesn’t apply to competitors’ prices or certain products excluded from the holiday return period, including items that require a third-party contract, like smartphones.

As of now, Walmart doesn’t price-match competitors, though Walmart stores will match prices on identical items sold at Walmart.com provided they’re in stock online.

However, the policy doesn’t apply to residents of Alaska, Hawaii, or Puerto Rico. Additionally, it doesn’t apply to special event prices, like those seen during Black Friday. Walmart also doesn’t retroactively price-match items purchased on Walmart.com that drop in price after the time of purchase. The retailer doesn’t price-match items purchased from Walmart Marketplace retailers or third-party sellers, either, and Walmart says the store manager on duty makes the final decision when you request a price match.

Apple doesn’t officially advertise a price-matching policy on its website. That said, if Apple reduces the price of an Apple-branded product within 14 days of when you receive it, you can visit an Apple Store or contact Apple Support at 1-800-MY-APPLE within 14 days of the price change to request a refund or credit for the difference. However, this doesn’t apply to special promotional pricing, such as Black Friday or Cyber Monday deals.

B&H says it may honor a current lower price or match a competitor’s price, but only on a case-by-case basis. You must contact its customer service team via on-site chat, email, or by calling 1-800-606-6969 / 1-212-444-6615. Then, if approved, B&H Photo will price match one identical item per customer.

Costco does not price-match competitors. However, according to its website, it will issue a credit for the difference between the price a member paid and the promotional price if the item drops in price within 30 days of purchase. For promotions with specific sale dates, such as holiday savings events, requests must be submitted while the promotion is active and within 30 days of purchase. If you bought the product at a Costco warehouse location, visit the membership counter at the store where you made the purchase. Costco doesn’t price-match items purchased at Costco warehouses with items purchased on Costco.com.

Dell will price-match identical products from Dell, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, HP, Apple, Lenovo, and several other retailers. Dell will not match prices available at Costco or Sam’s Club. You can call 1-877-275-3355 or chat online to run a price check, but you’ll need to provide a link to the competitor’s product. Dell outlines the specs you’ll need to compare to determine whether an item is eligible for a price match before you contact them, and before you make a purchase.

Normally, you can request a price adjustment within 30 days of purchase. For the holidays, Dell has extended that window for eligible PCs, monitors, and accessories purchased on Dell.com between November 1st and December 29th. You can request a price adjustment through January 15th, 2027, or within 30 days of the invoice date, whichever is later.

eBay doesn’t offer price matching on purchases made during the week of Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, but it does provide a generous price guarantee on select items outside that window. If you buy an item marked with the “Best Price Guarantee” badge — or one featured in eBay Deals — and find a lower price from an approved competitor within 48 hours, eBay will give you 110 percent of the price difference in the form of a coupon. That means you’ll receive a coupon worth the full difference plus an extra 10 percent, which you can use toward your next eBay purchase. Approved competitors include Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and Walmart.

The products must be new, unopened, and identical to the competitor’s item. You must contact eBay Customer Service, and if they verify your claims are legitimate, you’ll receive a coupon that’s good toward your next eBay purchase. However, you can only price-match one item per day.

GameStop claims its website will automatically match competitor pricing to offer shoppers the best available price. However, according to its official policy, the retailer doesn’t offer additional price matching beyond the prices already displayed on its website.

If you make a request within the standard window or the holiday return period, Google will match online pricing from select retailers — specifically Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, B&H Photo, Signifi, and Target. It doesn’t, however, match preorder pricing from other retailers or carrier deals. The product must also be in stock and identical, right down to the color and configuration. You also need to provide a public link to the promo page or product listing to verify the lower price, and the item must be in stock. Items sold by third-party sellers are ineligible for a price match.

Amazon Prime deals are eligible for price matching, but other members-only discounts aren’t. Other exclusions apply, too, including wholesale and educational pricing; mail-in offers and coupons; product bundles; clearance, open-box, refurbished, and pre-owned items; and products sold by third-party sellers on a competitor’s website. Google will only provide a price match on smartphones and other products with data plans if they’re unlocked devices.

You may also receive the difference if the product you purchased from the Google Store drops in price within the standard or holiday return period, though you’ll need to contact Google directly to get the price match or correction.

The Home Depot will match the price of identical, in-stock products from other retailers, except for membership-based wholesalers. The retailer must be able to ship the item to your location, so prices from regional retailers are ineligible. The price-match policy does not apply to special events like Black Friday, clearance prices, used and refurbished items, or rebate offers. You may request a price match within 30 days of your purchase.

You must bring the ad or listing to the register in-store. (You can also request price matches for online purchases that are shipped to the customer.) For online orders, you’ll need to provide the exact SKU for the item on both the competitor’s and The Home Depot’s sites. To request a price match by phone, you can call 1-800-430-3376. Additionally, The Home Depot will honor requests only from the original buyer.

According to HP’s website, the company will match the current pre-tax price for new comparable PCs and identical HP printer, display, and accessory model numbers from nationally recognized online retailers, such as Dell, Lenovo, Amazon, Staples, Newegg, and Best Buy. Item specs must be identical to get a price match, but the product model number does not need to be exact.

You must ask for the match at the time of purchase by calling 1-800-888-0229 or via chat. You can’t request a price match via email, and the policy doesn’t apply to items purchased during promotional periods. It also doesn’t apply to membership stores like Costco and Sam’s Club, items purchased through a third-party vendor on an approved site, or items purchased using financing.

HP also offers price protection on HP-branded products. If a price drops during your 30-day return window, you can request an adjustment by contacting HP’s Order Support team. This doesn’t apply to products purchased during certain seasonal sales events, including Fourth of July promotions and deals offered during the week of Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday.

Lenovo matches pricing on comparable PCs from Lenovo, HP, or Dell with the same key specs as long as they’re sold through a list of recognized retailers. That list includes bigger stores such as Best Buy, Walmart, Amazon, Newegg, and B&H Photo, as well as direct competitors such as Dell and HP. The comparable PC must also be in stock and readily available from both Lenovo and the competing retailer, and you must contact a Lenovo sales rep with specific details about the specs and availability of the product you’re inquiring about in order to facilitate the match.

That said, you can’t use coupons or special discounts when requesting a price match, and the policy doesn’t apply to membership stores like Costco. The policy also doesn’t apply to “Marketplace” items fulfilled by third parties, so double-check that you bought the product directly from the retailer. Build-your-own models are also ineligible for a price match. Lenovo’s separate Price Guarantee program, meanwhile, is limited to five eligible Lenovo products per customer per year.

Lenovo also offers a price guarantee refund for laptops and personal desktop computers bought from Lenovo.com within 30 days of purchase. To receive a refund, you must contact Customer Care and provide proof of the lower price for the identical product offered on Lenovo.com. This policy doesn’t apply to doorbuster or clearance products, however.

For the holidays, Lenovo has extended its price guarantee through January 27th, 2027, for eligible purchases made between November 2nd and December 13th. To request an adjustment, email a dated screenshot of the lower price to “na_lpg@lenovo.com” by January 27th.

Lowe’s will match the price of identical, in-stock products when you present an ad, product listing, or photo from a qualifying online or local retailer, including Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and Walmart. However, the product must be purchased directly from the retailer and not a third-party seller; it also doesn’t apply to special sales events like Black Friday and other holiday promotions.

Additionally, Lowe’s doesn’t match prices from one Lowe’s store to another, nor does it match any rebate discounts or those available only to a select group of customers (such as loyalty clubs). Clearance, seasonal, buy one get one free, and custom-made items are also ineligible for a price match. To request a price match, you can go to the store, call 1-877-465-6937, or chat online.

Normally, Microsoft will refund the difference if it drops the price of an in-stock physical product purchased online from the Microsoft Store within 60 days of delivery. For the holidays, however, Microsoft has extended that window through January 31st, 2027, for eligible purchases made between October 1st and December 2nd. The same 60-day policy also applies if you find the identical product on sale at a lower price at a qualifying retailer such as Amazon or Best Buy, though it doesn’t extend to the Surface Hub, HoloLens, Windows DevKits, or digital products.

Furthermore, some eligible products are subject to specific retailer exclusions. For example, price matches for Surface products at other retailers are limited to Amazon and Best Buy, while Xbox products are limited to those two retailers, as well as Target, GameStop, and Walmart. The price match policy excludes products from third-party sellers, clearance items, bundles, rebates, and prices only available after guests log in.

You’ll need to contact Microsoft’s Sales and Support team at 1-800-642-7676 within 60 days of delivery to request a refund, unless your purchase qualifies for the extended holiday price protection period. If you purchase an item from a Microsoft Experience Center, you’ll need to return to that location with your receipt. In both cases, Microsoft will credit the difference between the price you paid and the current lower price to your original payment method, which typically takes between three and five days to process.

Newegg no longer matches prices from competing retailers. The company only price matches eligible items sold and shipped by Newegg (not third-party sellers), and the product must be identical and in stock. The lower price must also appear on Newegg.com within seven calendar days of your purchase. If approved, Newegg will issue the difference as credit you can use on the site or in the app for up to 365 days.

The match doesn’t apply to rebates, coupons, financing offers, bundles, clearance items, open-box items, or refurbished products. The policy also doesn’t apply to prices found at third-party marketplace sellers, or products on sale during major sales events like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

You can currently request a price match against other Sam’s Club stores, but not competitors. Note that this doesn’t apply to items marked down or on clearance.
